entries.name: Salesforce Hosted MCP Servers
entries.summary: Salesforce runs MCP servers that let an AI assistant read (and, where an admin allows it, change) a Salesforce org's records as the person who signed in, with that person's object, field and sharing permissions. Two standard servers are confirmed: platform/sobject-reads (read-only, includes getUserInfo) and platform/sobject-all (read, create, update and delete, plus prompt templates). Admins can also build custom servers from Apex actions, Flows and Named Queries.
details: The servers run no AI model themselves, and every tool call counts against the org's daily API request quota.
entries.tradecomply_role: Add Salesforce's hosted MCP server and TradeComply's MCP server to the same AI assistant. The assistant pulls subcontractor Accounts or bid Opportunities from Salesforce and runs TradeComply's California checks on them. TradeComply never holds your Salesforce sign-in.

uses.text: In Claude with both connectors attached, run soqlQuery on platform/sobject-reads to pull the Accounts the GC tracks as subcontractors, with their CSLB license-number field (the field name is specific to each org). Pass the list to TradeComply bulk_check_subcontractors to flag expired licenses, missing workers' comp or classification problems before an award.

When a bid Opportunity with a city, county, school district or Caltrans agency goes Closed Won, run TradeComply public_works_readiness, project_setup_checklist and, if federal money is involved, davis_bacon_vs_ca_prevailing. Then, with platform/sobject-all enabled, use createSobjectRecord to log the pre-start checklist as a Task on the Opportunity.

For residential remodel leads in Salesforce, draft the contract from the Opportunity scope and price with generate_home_improvement_contract, check it with validate_home_improvement_contract, and write the home_improvement_cancellation_deadline date back to the Opportunity with updateSobjectRecord (needs sobject-all).

Turn TradeComply compliance_calendar, calculate_lien_deadline and stop_payment_notice_deadline dates into Salesforce Tasks owned by the project manager, so lien and notice deadlines appear in the CRM the office already uses.
Before creating a new trade-partner Account, run verify_contractor_license and check_subcontractor_compliance in the same chat and paste the result into the Account description.

mcp.note: Endpoints are built per org and per server on api.salesforce.com. Common errors: 404 means the server is not activated; 401 means wrong scopes or the External Client App has not propagated yet (changes can take up to 30 minutes).

servers.label: platform/sobject-reads (read-only)
servers.auth: OAuth 2.0 authorization code with PKCE through an External Client App your Salesforce admin creates (Setup > External Client App Manager), with scopes mcp_api and refresh_token and 'Issue JWT-based access tokens for named users' turned on. Connected Apps are not supported.
servers.notes: The plain URL is the production / Developer Edition form. Salesforce recommends the My Domain form (required when login.salesforce.com login is disabled). Sandboxes use https://api.salesforce.com/platform/mcp/v1/sandbox/{servername}. Servers are off until an admin turns each on (Setup > API Catalog > MCP Servers). The mcp-remote bridge is not supported. Connection check: call getUserInfo.

servers.label: platform/sobject-all (read and write)
servers.auth: Same External Client App sign-in as sobject-reads.
servers.notes: Acts with the signed-in user's full permissions, and Salesforce's audit trail shows that user as the editor. Start with sobject-reads.

api.auth: OAuth 2.0 authorization code + PKCE only; no service-account or machine-to-machine flow.
notes: Recommended use: connect Salesforce's hosted MCP and TradeComply's /mcp side by side in the customer's AI client.

A server-side TradeComply connector is technically possible without partner approval, because each customer admin can create an External Client App. Its limits: a person must sign in (no unattended sync); refresh tokens would need per-tenant encrypted storage; External Client App changes can take up to 30 minutes to propagate; server activation can take up to 2 minutes; Experience Cloud custom-domain URLs are not supported.
A plain REST connector would use the Salesforce REST API instead of MCP. Its endpoint and version details were not re-read in our 2026-11-26 research; confirm them before building.
Pricing: none found. One third-party source mentions Flex Credits; unconfirmed.

gov.name: Salesforce Government Cloud Plus
gov.note: Salesforce's 'Use Agentforce Vibes with Government Cloud Orgs' page lists Hosted MCP Servers as not yet supported in Government Cloud. That page is undated, so recheck it before telling a Government Cloud customer either way. Government Cloud Plus runs on AWS GovCloud (US) (FedRAMP High, now labeled FedRAMP Class D, plus DoD IL2).
gov.label: Government cloud: not available

status.label: Generally available
status.note: GA per Salesforce's developer blog dated 2026-04-29 (Enterprise Edition and above; Developer Edition orgs can also use it). Pilot in spring 2025, beta in October 2025. At GA the URL version changed from v1-beta.2 to v1 and activation became per server.

caveats: Write access (sobject-all) acts with the signed-in user's full permissions, and the audit trail shows that user as the editor. Start customers on sobject-reads.
MCP calls use the org's daily API request quota (Setup > Company Information > API Requests, Last 24 Hours).
The list of standard servers beyond sobject-reads and sobject-all, and their tool names, was not confirmed against the official servers reference.
Government Cloud: see the government note; the source page is undated.
research_notes: developer.salesforce.com and www.salesforce.com could not be fetched during our research. Blog and Government Cloud facts come from web-search extraction of those pages. URL patterns, scopes and limits come from Salesforce's official GitHub repo forcedotcom/mcp-hosted (README and wiki), which we read directly.

entries.name: ServiceNow MCP Server Console
entries.summary: ServiceNow's MCP Server Console (introduced in the Zurich release, shipped as a ServiceNow Store app) lets AI assistants reach governed functions on your own ServiceNow instance: incident and case lookup in the preconfigured Quickstart Server, plus tools admins build from Now Assist skills, Subflows, Actions, scripted REST APIs and knowledge graphs. Admins can require a role on each tool. It needs Now Assist and the Model Context Protocol Server plugin (snmcpserver).
entries.tradecomply_role: For a large GC that runs safety, HR or IT intake in ServiceNow: put ServiceNow's MCP server and TradeComply's in the same AI assistant so California deadlines and rules are checked against the case in front of you. ServiceNow is not a core construction system, so TradeComply has no built-in connector for it.

uses.text: For a large GC that runs safety and HR intake in ServiceNow: when the Quickstart Server surfaces a case describing a jobsite injury, run TradeComply injury_reporting_deadlines (Cal/OSHA serious-injury reporting clock) and jobsite_hazard_checklist in the same chat. Writing the deadline back to the case needs an admin-built tool (Subflow or scripted REST) exposed in MCP Server Console.

Use HR Service Delivery case data (an employee leave or termination request) with TradeComply leave_request_check, sick_leave_status and final_paycheck_deadline, so HR answers field-employee questions with California rules.

Read off-road equipment and truck asset records the GC keeps in ServiceNow asset tables through a custom MCP tool, then run offroad_fleet_obligations, portable_engine_requirements and truck_compliance on the fleet list.
When a new subcontractor onboarding request comes through the service catalog, run bulk_check_subcontractors or check_subcontractor_compliance on the license numbers in the request.
Turn compliance_calendar output into ServiceNow tasks for the safety and HR teams. This needs a write tool built in MCP Server Console.

mcp.note: A ServiceNow community forum report says ServiceNow uses pre-registered clients and offers no dynamic client registration, so AI clients that only support dynamic registration fail.

servers.label: Quickstart Server (on your instance)
servers.auth: OAuth (ServiceNow docs reference OAuth 2.1). An admin with oauth_admin, mi_admin or admin creates one OAuth inbound integration per MCP client: manual client registration, Authorization Code grant, Client Secret Post. Authorization URL https://<instance>.service-now.com/oauth_auth.do; token URL https://<instance>.service-now.com/oauth_token.do.
servers.notes: Copy the exact URL from the server record in MCP Server Console > Configuration > Servers; a server must be activated first. Other servers follow https://<instance>.service-now.com/sncapps/mcp-server/mcp/<server-name>.

api.auth: OAuth inbound integration on the customer's instance.
notes: Not recommended as a built-in TradeComply connector: the MCP server sits on each customer's instance and needs Now Assist licensing.

If ever needed, direct REST is possible without partner approval: the customer creates an OAuth inbound integration and tokens come from POST https://<instance>.service-now.com/oauth_token.do. The inbound client-credentials grant needs the system property glide.oauth.inbound.client.credential.grant_type.enabled=true and an OAuth Application User (per an AWS Bedrock setup guide and ServiceNow's client-credentials docs, found via search). Community threads conflict on whether client credentials work for inbound Table API calls, so test on a personal developer instance first.
The Table API request and response shapes were not re-read in our 2026-11-26 research.

Whether MCP Server Console runs in GCC is unconfirmed; ask your ServiceNow account team (KB1584492 is cited for availability).

entries.name: Deltek Costpoint (Dela MCP server)
entries.summary: Costpoint is Deltek's project ERP for government contractors: DCAA-oriented timekeeping, labor and cost segregation, indirect rates, billing and audit trails. Since release 2026.3, its AI assistant Dela can act as an MCP server, so authorized AI clients can query Costpoint as the signed-in user under their Costpoint security roles. Microsoft also lists a 'Deltek Costpoint (Preview)' connector for Copilot Studio, Power Automate, Power Apps and Logic Apps.
entries.tradecomply_role: For a California contractor doing federal work booked in Costpoint: connect Costpoint's MCP server and TradeComply's in the same AI assistant, so labor hours from Costpoint can be checked against California and federal wage rules. Without the MCP add-on, export reports as CSV instead.

uses.text: For a California contractor on a federal job (for example Army Corps or NAVFAC work booked in Costpoint): ask Dela through Costpoint MCP for weekly labor hours by employee and labor category, then run TradeComply check_payroll and davis_bacon_vs_ca_prevailing to see whether the federal or California prevailing rate controls each classification.
Run federal_overtime_exposure on the same timesheet hours (contract work hours overtime exposure), and prevailing_wage_penalties to price any underpayment before a certified-payroll correction.
Before issuing POs on a federally funded project tracked in Costpoint, run federal_project_requirements and buy_america_check on the material list.
Compare Costpoint fringe and indirect rates with TradeComply labor_burden_estimate, and check apprentice_hours_required against Costpoint labor hours on public works.

(Unconfirmed, beta) Register TradeComply's /mcp endpoint in Costpoint's outbound 'MCP Servers (Beta)' subtask with the API Key authorization type, so Ask Dela can call TradeComply tools from inside Costpoint. The header format for the API Key type was not documented in what we found, and activation may need a Deltek support ticket.

servers.label: Dela MCP server (your Costpoint tenant)
servers.auth: OAuth with dynamic client registration (per Microsoft's connector page). On first connection a sign-in page asks for the Costpoint tenant ID, then the Costpoint user ID and password.
servers.notes: No public fixed URL: Costpoint shows it under Configure System Settings > Dela tab > 'MCP URI'. A Trusted MCP Clients subtask controls which AI clients may connect.

api.auth: Customer-specific web-service credentials.
notes: Not a built-in candidate. Deltek's Costpoint developer-resources page says the Costpoint API runs over SOAP/XML, REST/XML and REST/JSON, and states 'There is no reference documentation'. Cloud web-service integrations need customer-specific values (Web Service URL, User, Database Name, Client ID, Client Secret), per Deltek's TIP setup guide.
Per the 2026.2 release notes, activating MCP server integration may need a Deltek Support ticket.
Fallback: export timesheet or labor-distribution reports from Costpoint as CSV and use them with check_payroll and davis_bacon_vs_ca_prevailing.

gov.name: Costpoint GovCon Cloud Moderate (GCCM)
gov.note: GCCM has FedRAMP Moderate Ready status (renewed under Rev 5 in February 2025), and Deltek reports FedRAMP Moderate Equivalency. Whether the Dela MCP add-on is available in GCCM is unconfirmed. Microsoft's 'Deltek Costpoint' connector is not available in US Government GCC, GCC High, DoD or China clouds.
gov.label: Government cloud: unconfirmed

status.label: Preview
status.note: Microsoft connector: 'Deltek Costpoint (Preview)', Premium, publisher Deltek. Costpoint 2026.3 (build 2026.3.0.5017, dated 2026-07-15) says Dela can now operate as an MCP server. 2026.2 added an outbound 'MCP Servers (Beta)' integration where Dela calls third-party MCP servers (No Auth, API Key or OAuth).

caveats: Search results say connecting Dela to third-party tools through MCP is a separately licensed add-on for Deltek Cloud customers only, while the 2026.3 notes also describe IIS rewrite rules for on-premises web servers. These conflict; confirm licensing and deployment scope with Deltek.
Costpoint is aimed mainly at government contractors. Few California GC or sub offices run it unless they do substantial federal work.
The exact Dela MCP tool list is not published in what we found ('supported workflows' only).
research_notes: learn.microsoft.com, help.deltek.com and www.deltek.com could not be fetched during our research. All Costpoint facts come from web-search extraction of those official pages.

entries.name: Ivalua (source-to-pay)
entries.summary: Ivalua is a source-to-pay suite: supplier management, sourcing, contracts, purchasing, invoicing and payments, with a packaged edition for construction and engineering firms since 2020. Its AI agent IVA is governed through IVA Studio (launched in beta on 2026-06-11), inherits the invoking user's permissions and logs its actions.
details: Ivalua names construction customers such as Strabag, Eiffage, LeFrak, Vinci, NCC and John Holland (vendor statements).
entries.tradecomply_role: Export your approved-supplier list from Ivalua as CSV and import it into TradeComply (Subs > Import), which checks every CSLB license. Send the results back to the supplier record as a document. Ivalua describes a hosted MCP server, but there is no public endpoint to connect yet.

uses.text: Export the approved-supplier list (company name, CSLB license number) from Ivalua supplier management as CSV and POST it to TradeComply /api/subs/import, which returns the risk report. Re-run bulk_check_subcontractors monthly and attach the PDF or JSON result to the supplier record in Ivalua.

During supplier onboarding for a trade package, run verify_contractor_license, classification_for_scope (does the sub's CSLB classification cover the scope?) and certifications_required before the supplier is approved.

Before approving a subcontractor invoice in Ivalua's purchase-to-pay flow, run prompt_payment_check, retention_cap_check and select_lien_waiver, so the right conditional or unconditional waiver comes in with the payment.
For a sourcing event on federally funded materials, run buy_america_check on the bill of materials before award.
For public works packages, run public_works_readiness to confirm DIR registration and readiness for each bidding sub.

mcp.note: Ivalua's integrations page reportedly describes a hosted MCP server, but no official endpoint or setup guide is public.

api.auth: Unconfirmed: Ivalua's API reference is customer-only.
notes: Not a built-in candidate: Ivalua's API reference is customer-only, and we found no self-serve developer program or published auth flow.

Integration path: CSV export from Ivalua into TradeComply POST /api/subs/import (multipart field 'file', a text/csv body, or JSON {"csv": ...}; Authorization: Bearer <TradeComply API key>). Results go back to Ivalua by document upload.
Revisit if Ivalua publishes its hosted MCP endpoint; customers could then attach it next to TradeComply in their AI client.

status.label: Beta (IVA Studio)
status.note: IVA Studio was announced at Ivalua NOW (Paris) in March 2026 and launched in beta on 2026-06-11. GA was reportedly planned for summer 2026; we found no confirmation that it happened. The one documented MCP integration is outbound (Dun & Bradstreet risk data).

caveats: Ivalua mostly serves large enterprises and big contractors. Typical California GC or sub offices are unlikely to run it.
No US government or FedRAMP variant was found.
research_notes: All MCP claims come from Ivalua's own marketing pages and press release, reached only through web-search extraction (www.ivalua.com could not be fetched). The endpoint, transport, GA status and auth details are unverified.

A third-party probe (apis.io) reports an OAuth protected-resource document on portal.ivalua.com naming a /mcp URL with one scope, offline_access. That is not Ivalua documentation, so it is not listed as an endpoint; a real deployment is probably per customer.
A third-party review checked 2026-09-27 found no public Ivalua MCP endpoint, developer page or setup guide, and no Ivalua entry in the official MCP registry.

entries.name: Workato Enterprise MCP
entries.summary: Workato is an automation (iPaaS) platform. Its Enterprise MCP turns Workato recipes, API collections and connectors into governed MCP servers, ships prebuilt MCP servers for SaaS apps (Workato names Slack, DocuSign, QuickBooks Online and ServiceNow ITSM among them), and lets Workato Genies call outside MCP servers, with an Enterprise MCP Registry for approved servers. Workato also has a 'Procore Official' connector for recipes.
entries.tradecomply_role: Workato calls TradeComply, so nothing is installed on TradeComply's side. Add TradeComply's /mcp to a Genie as a custom MCP server, or call TradeComply's REST API from a recipe, using a dedicated TradeComply API key stored in a Workato connection (never in recipe text).

uses.text: Recipe: a Procore Official connector trigger on a new or updated vendor company calls TradeComply POST https://missed-call-recovery-n1c3.onrender.com/api/subs/import (Authorization: Bearer <TradeComply API key> kept in a Workato connection). Failing rows from the returned bulk_check_subcontractors-style risk report are posted to a Slack channel.

Add TradeComply's /mcp as a custom MCP server on a Workato Genie (token-header auth) next to Workato's prebuilt DocuSign MCP server. The Genie runs generate_home_improvement_contract, checks it with validate_home_improvement_contract, and sends it for signature through DocuSign.

A weekly scheduled recipe calls TradeComply POST /api/tools/compliance_calendar for each active project and posts upcoming Cal/OSHA, lien and payroll deadlines to Slack through Workato's prebuilt Slack MCP server or Slack connector.

Before a subcontractor payment goes out through the QuickBooks Online AP & Expenses prebuilt MCP server, the Genie runs prompt_payment_check, retention_cap_check and select_lien_waiver and blocks the payment if a waiver is missing.

Enterprise IT lists TradeComply in the Workato Enterprise MCP Registry and limits which of its read-only tools each Genie may call (for example only verify_contractor_license and calculate_lien_deadline for the estimating team).

mcp.note: Workato's Microsoft Copilot example uses protocol 'mcp-streamable-1.0' (Streamable HTTP).

servers.label: Your Enterprise MCP servers (per workspace)
servers.auth: Token by default (generated in MCP server settings; sent as the wkt_token query parameter or a header). Alternative: OAuth 2.0 through Workato Identity; switching revokes the token and every client must be reconfigured.
servers.notes: Generated per workspace and per server: copy the URL from AI Hub > Enterprise MCP > Custom servers > server details.

servers.label: Developer and Embedded API MCP server (US data center)
servers.auth: Token or OAuth, as configured in Workato.
servers.notes: Other data centers use app.<region>.workato.com/mcp/ (EU, JP, SG, AU, IL, KR, UK) and https://app.workatoapp.cn/mcp/ (CN). Seen only through search extracts of Workato's docs.

api.auth: Workato stores the TradeComply API key in a Workato connection.
notes: Paths on TradeComply's side: (1) a Workato Genie adds TradeComply's /mcp URL as a custom MCP server (Streamable HTTP, header 'Authorization: Bearer <TradeComply API key>' using Workato's token-header option); (2) Workato recipes use the HTTP connector against /api/tools/{name} and /api/subs/import with the same key.

Token mode is one shared auth context, so every Genie user shares one TradeComply key. Create a dedicated, revocable 'Workato' key per company so TradeComply's activity log can tell it apart. Calls arrive from Workato's servers, because external MCP requests are proxied through Workato.

status.label: Available
status.note: Workato announced Enterprise MCP as available on 2025-10-01 and for SaaS platforms on 2025-10-28. Later GA entries: MCP Apps (2026-06-08); MCP Registry, Multi-Token Auth and Tool Annotation Support (2026-08-11). Per Workato's FAQ, MCP runs in the US, EU, AU, SG and JP data centers. Pricing is by quote only.

caveats: Search found no single platform-wide GA date; both the 2025 launch language and the per-feature GA entries are reported above.
The prebuilt-server catalog changes often and differs across Workato pages; confirm current servers in your AI Hub. A Procore prebuilt MCP server was not found, only the Procore recipe connector.
Workato's FAQ wording on API-collection support for Verified User Access is inconsistent; check it before relying on per-user auth.
No FedRAMP or US-government variant of Workato was checked or found.
research_notes: docs.workato.com and www.workato.com could not be fetched during our research. Every Workato fact comes from web-search extraction of the official docs and changelog pages.

entries.name: Procore
entries.summary: Procore is the construction management platform many mid-size and large GCs and owners use: projects, the company directory (vendors), commitments (subcontracts and purchase orders), daily logs, timesheets and timecards, documents, RFIs and submittals. It has a public REST API with OAuth 2.0, webhooks, a Developer Portal with sandboxes, and an App Marketplace. Procore bought Datagrid in January 2026 and is embedding Datagrid agents as Procore AI.
details: Procore's own compliance features: vendor insurance records in the Company and Project Directory (the insurance manager gets emails starting 2 weeks before a policy expires and daily for up to 60 days after; status turns non-compliant within 24 hours of expiry), a Procore Pay compliance tab on commitments, Procore Prequalification (Procore's blog says it sunsets March 31, 2027, naming COMPASS by Bespoke Metrics as the preferred replacement) and lien rights through Levelset, sold separately.

TradeComply adds the California-specific checks Procore does not do: CSLB license, classification and workers' comp checks from the vendor license_number, classification-to-scope matching, unlicensed-contracting exposure, Cal/OSHA written programs and permits, California wage rules on timecards, lien, stop-payment and prompt-payment deadlines, and DIR public-works readiness.
entries.tradecomply_role: TradeComply's built-in Procore connection signs in to your Procore company with OAuth so TradeComply's California checks can run on the Procore data they need, starting with the vendor directory's license numbers. Procore access is governed by the tool permissions you grant the app.

builtin.what_it_does: Connects one Procore company with OAuth. Planned uses: re-check every vendor's CSLB license from the Procore directory, check approved subcontracts against the sub's license classes, and read timecards and accident logs for California wage and Cal/OSHA reporting checks.

uses.text: Nightly, pull the Company Directory (GET /rest/v1.0/vendors?company_id=…). Send each vendor's license_number and name to bulk_check_subcontractors, and flag suspended or expired CSLB licenses and missing workers' comp before the PM issues a new subcontract.

For each approved subcontract (GET /rest/v1.0/work_order_contracts?project_id=…&filters[status]=Approved), run classification_for_scope against the sub's CSLB classes and the contract scope. Then run check_subcontractor_compliance, and unlicensed_contracting_exposure when the license does not cover the work.

Compare Procore's vendor insurance records (expiration dates entered by hand) with verify_contractor_license output (CSLB workers' comp policy or exemption on file). This catches subs whose COI in Procore is current but whose CSLB record shows a workers' comp suspension or exemption.

Pull timecard entries (GET /rest/v1.0/projects/{project_id}/timecard_entries; time_in, time_out, lunch_time, hours, date). Run check_payroll for California daily overtime and meal/rest timing. When a crew demobilizes, run final_paycheck_deadline.

Pull the day's accident logs (GET /rest/v1.0/projects/{project_id}/accident_logs?log_date=YYYY-MM-DD) and run injury_reporting_deadlines, so the Cal/OSHA serious-injury report and the 5020 deadlines go on the safety manager's list right away.
Compare manpower-log companies on site against the subs that passed bulk_check_subcontractors. Any company on site without a clean check gets a check_subcontractor_compliance review the same day.

For each Procore project (GET /rest/v1.0/projects?company_id=…), seed TradeComply with project_setup_checklist, permit_required and public_works_readiness (DIR registration and certified payroll if public). Then generate compliance_calendar, plus calculate_lien_deadline for preliminary notices.

Upload the IIPP, heat illness and WVPP from generate_safety_programs, or a signed home-improvement contract from generate_home_improvement_contract, into the project's Procore documents with the unified upload flow (POST /rest/v2.1/companies/{company_id}/projects/{project_id}/uploads, then PUT to the presigned URL). This is a write action that must be approved in the TradeComply web app; TradeComply's MCP tools stay read-only.

Register a company-level webhook (POST /rest/v1.0/webhooks/hooks, then add triggers) so a vendor create or update in Procore re-runs bulk_check_subcontractors. The exact trigger resource_name for vendors needs to be confirmed in the API reference.

Inside an AI client, a PM can use the Procore AI Edge MCP (procore_read) next to the TradeComply MCP, for example reading a project's RFIs and daily logs and then calling check_cal_osha_permits or jobsite_hazard_checklist on the scope. This depends on the customer having Datagrid access.

mcp.note: Community and third-party Procore MCP servers (Composio, Pipedream, CData and GitHub projects) are not Procore products and need the customer's own Procore OAuth app.

servers.label: Procore AI Edge MCP
servers.auth: A Datagrid API key sent as 'Authorization: Bearer dg_live_...' (not Procore OAuth). The Datagrid-Teamspace, procore-company-id and procore-project-id headers are optional.
servers.notes: Documented in Procore's official documentation repo; whether it is generally available is not stated. Needs a Datagrid account or teamspace (app.datagrid.com). Exposes generic tools (procore_read, procore_write, converse, health, whoami).

api.auth: OAuth 2.0 authorization code grant (with refresh token) for user-level access, or client credentials through a Developer Managed Service Account (DMSA) for system-level access with no refresh token. Every call also needs the Procore-Company-Id header.
notes: AUTH. Authorize: GET https://login.procore.com/oauth/authorize?client_id=…&response_type=code&redirect_uri=…&state=…. The authorization code is single-use and expires in 10 minutes. The docs show no OAuth scope parameter; access is governed by Procore tool permissions. Token: POST https://login.procore.com/oauth/token, form fields grant_type=authorization_code with client_id, client_secret, code and redirect_uri. Response: {access_token, token_type: "bearer", expires_in (5400 in the docs example), refresh_token, created_at}. Client credentials: grant_type=client_credentials with client_id and client_secret; no refresh_token, so request a new token when it expires.

DMSA SETUP. In the Developer Portal app, add Data Connector Components: Service Account Authentication plus User Level Authentication. Set company and project tool permissions in the Permissions Builder. A company admin installs the app from the Marketplace, or through Company Tools > Admin > App Management > Install App > Install Custom App using the App Version Key, and picks the permitted projects. A DMSA user is created in the company Directory. Custom (private) installs need no Marketplace listing, which is what makes a direct connector realistic without partner approval.

ENVIRONMENTS. Production: auth https://login.procore.com, API https://api.procore.com. Developer Sandbox: auth https://login-sandbox.procore.com, API https://sandbox.procore.com (sandbox OAuth credentials and the Sandbox App Version Key). Monthly Sandbox: auth https://login-sandbox-monthly.procore.com, API https://api-monthly.procore.com (production credentials and App Version Key). On-Demand Sandbox: production URLs, scoped by company_id. Tokens are not shared between production and sandbox.

HEADERS. Authorization: Bearer <token>. Procore-Company-Id: <id> on every call, even when company_id is also a query or path parameter; without it Procore returns 'Missing Procore-Company-Id header!'. For DMSA with multiple Procore regions, the header is mandatory on /rest/v1.0/me and /rest/v1.0/companies.

ENDPOINTS SEEN IN THE OFFICIAL DOCS. GET /rest/v1.0/me; GET /rest/v1.0/companies; GET /rest/v1.0/projects?company_id=…; GET /rest/v1.0/vendors?company_id=…&sort=name (fields include id, name, trade_name, license_number, is_active, prequalified, union_member, non_union_prevailing_wage, labor_union, origin_id, business_phone, email_address, state_code, vendor_group, attachments); Company Vendor Insurances (reference page developers.procore.com/reference/rest/v1/company-vendor-insurances; fields include policy number, insurance type, effective and expiration dates, limit and name; the URL path was not verified); GET /rest/v1.0/work_order_contracts?project_id=…&filters[status]=Approved; GET /rest/v1.0/purchase_order_contracts?project_id=…; daily logs GET /rest/v1.0/projects/{project_id}/accident_logs?log_date=YYYY-MM-DD or ?start_date=&end_date= (with no date filter only today's logs return); timecards /rest/v1.0/projects/{project_id}/timesheets and /timecard_entries; uploads POST /rest/v2.1/companies/{company_id}/projects/{project_id}/uploads returning segments[].url, then PUT the bytes to each presigned URL; webhooks POST /rest/v1.0/webhooks/hooks {company_id|project_id, hook: {api_version: 'v2', namespace, destination_url, destination_headers}} then POST /rest/v1.0/webhooks/hooks/{hook_id}/triggers {company_id, api_version: 'v2', trigger: {resource_name, event_type: create|update|delete}}.
PAGINATION. Query parameters page and per_page. Response headers Link (first/prev/next/last), Total and Per-Page. v2 collections default to 10 per page, maximum 100.

RATE LIMITS. Two limits: hourly (60-minute window) and spike (10-second window). Headers X-Rate-Limit-Limit, X-Rate-Limit-Remaining and X-Rate-Limit-Reset (Unix seconds). Exceeding either returns 429; sleep until the reset time and back off with jitter. The docs example shows 600 but says not to assume a fixed number.

MARKETPLACE LISTING (optional). Partner Application at developers.procore.com/partner-signup, partner vetting, the Procore Framework Agreement and Technology Partner Addendum (no redlines), validation with a customer, a Marketplace Listing (screenshots, icons, descriptions, pricing) and demo video, then a final review against the Marketplace Approval Checklist.

IMPLEMENTATION. Keep TradeComply's Procore client_id and client_secret in environment variables. Per tenant, store the Procore company_id and permitted projects; store user refresh tokens encrypted. Tests mock POST /oauth/token and GET /rest/v1.0/vendors (JSON array with Link/Total/Per-Page and X-Rate-Limit-* headers), including a 429 and a missing Procore-Company-Id case.

status.note: REST API: GA (Procore's Agentic APIs page labels REST APIs 'GA'). Agentic APIs (Converse API, on Datagrid): Design Partner pilot since March 2026, GA 'in development'. Declaring external MCP servers in an app manifest and an Agent Marketplace: 'in development'. Procore AI Edge MCP: no GA, beta or preview label seen. Embedded Datagrid AI: private beta per the May 21, 2026 press release. Procore AI connecting to third-party MCP servers is Enterprise-only, per a Procore support page (via search).

entries.name: Atlassian Rovo MCP Server (Jira and Confluence)
entries.summary: Atlassian's hosted MCP server (formerly the Atlassian Remote MCP Server) connects AI assistants to an Atlassian Cloud site: Jira, Confluence, Jira Service Management, Bitbucket Cloud, Compass, Loom and platform data. Tools come in permission groups such as read_jira, write_jira, search_jira, read_confluence and write_confluence (delete_jira and manage_jira are off by default). Access follows each user's existing permissions, and every tool call writes an audit-log event.
entries.tradecomply_role: For offices that track work in Jira or Confluence: add Rovo and TradeComply to the same AI assistant to turn TradeComply deadlines and sub problems into Jira issues, or publish safety programs to Confluence. Most California GC and sub offices are not on Jira, so TradeComply has no built-in Jira connector.

uses.text: In one AI-client session, run compliance_calendar for a project (preliminary notices, Cal/OSHA permit renewals, certified-payroll weeks). Then use the Rovo MCP write_jira tools to create a Jira issue per deadline, assigned to the PM with the due date set.

Turn each failing row from bulk_check_subcontractors (suspended license, workers' comp lapse) into a Jira ticket in a 'Sub Compliance' project. Close it when verify_contractor_license comes back clean.
Publish the IIPP, heat illness and WVPP text from generate_safety_programs to a controlled Confluence safety space with write_confluence, so field supervisors read one current version.

Read the job's scope from a Confluence page with read_confluence. Then call permit_required, energy_compliance_triggers and check_cal_osha_permits on it and post the results as a comment on the job page.

Run an internal compliance help desk in Jira Service Management (Rovo MCP needs API-token auth for this). A field request such as 'is this sub OK to start Monday?' gets answered with check_subcontractor_compliance and the citation pasted into the request.

mcp.note: Admins get domain allowlists (for OAuth), honoring of IP allowlists, app revocation, and an audit-log event for every tool call.

servers.label: Rovo MCP Server
servers.auth: OAuth 2.1 browser sign-in for interactive clients. For headless use an org admin must first allow API tokens (Atlassian Administration > Rovo > Rovo MCP server > Authentication); then send a personal API token as 'Authorization: Basic base64(email:api_token)' or a service-account key as 'Authorization: Bearer <key>'. Jira Service Management tools need API-token auth; Compass tools need OAuth.
servers.notes: Recommended endpoint. The v1 endpoints https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/mcp and https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/mcp/authv2 still work; the legacy SSE endpoint https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/sse is unsupported after 30 June 2026.

api.auth: Jira Cloud REST API v3 with OAuth 2.0 (3LO), or Basic auth with email and API token.
notes: A direct Jira connector is optional and lower priority. Jira Cloud REST API v3; non-Forge integrations use OAuth 2.0 (3LO) authorization code, authorizing at https://auth.atlassian.com/authorize. Request URLs: https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/{cloudId}/rest/api/3/{resource}. Classic scopes include read:jira-work and write:jira-work; granular scopes such as write:issue:jira also exist.

Create issue: POST /rest/api/3/issue. Bulk create: POST /rest/api/3/issue/bulk, up to 50 issues. description and textarea custom fields take Atlassian Document Format (ADF), not plain text. Alternative: Basic auth with email:API token against https://{site}.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/….
The token endpoint, the accessible-resources (cloudId) lookup and rate limits were not verified in our 2026-11-26 research.

The Rovo MCP server is hosted on commercial cloud at mcp.atlassian.com, and nothing found shows it is available in Government Cloud or inside the FedRAMP boundary. Do not use it for federal CUI.

entries.name: Kahua
entries.summary: Kahua calls itself an AI enterprise construction platform for complex capital programs, used mostly by owners, program managers and public agencies. It is built on kBuilder, a low-code app platform, and its AI assistant Noa launched on 2026-05-13. Kahua says it holds FedRAMP authorization and, per its June 2, 2026 press release, federal approval to run AI inside that boundary.
entries.tradecomply_role: Most California GCs and subs meet Kahua as a document portal on owner-run jobs. Generate the compliance packet in TradeComply and upload it to the owner's Kahua workflow by hand. There is no public API documentation or MCP server, so TradeComply has no direct connection.

uses.text: When a public owner runs its capital program in Kahua and requires the GC to upload compliance documents, generate the packet in TradeComply and upload it by hand. The packet includes public_works_readiness (DIR registration, certified payroll), apprentice_hours_required and a bulk_check_subcontractors report for every listed sub.
For federal or military work managed in Kahua's FedRAMP environment, prepare federal_project_requirements, davis_bacon_vs_ca_prevailing and buy_america_check outputs as submittal attachments.
Before a payment application goes into the owner's Kahua workflow, check retention and payment timing with retention_cap_check and prompt_payment_check, and pick lien waivers with select_lien_waiver.

mcp.note: No MCP server has been announced (searches found none).

api.auth: Unconfirmed: Kahua markets an 'open API', but no public API reference or auth documentation was found.
notes: Integrations are built on Kahua's open API by Kahua, partners and customers (one example is Clark Construction's SAP integration). A direct connector would need Kahua or customer cooperation, so it is not a built-in candidate.

gov.name: Kahua FedRAMP environment
gov.note: Kahua says its platform is FedRAMP authorized and approved to run AI inside that boundary (vendor press release). FedRAMP Marketplace status was not checked. TradeComply's path here is file upload, so no Kahua API is involved.
gov.label: Government cloud: unconfirmed

status.label: Current product
status.note: Noa (AI assistant) launched 2026-05-13 per Kahua's news page. No MCP server announced.

caveats: No public Kahua API documentation, auth method, rate limits or developer portal was found.
The FedRAMP claims come from Kahua and its press releases; FedRAMP Marketplace status was not checked.
Kahua's comparison page says the former e-Builder is now Trimble Unity Construct, which is a different vendor and API.

entries.name: Planisware (Enterprise and Orchestra)

Orchestra is the mid-market SaaS edition. Planisware says its MCP support connects its assistant Oscar and outside agents to Planisware for customers on version 26Q2 and above.
entries.tradecomply_role: Uncommon among 5 to 50 person California contractors. For a large owner or engineering firm on Planisware, export TradeComply results as CSV for import as portfolio risks or milestones.

uses.text: For a large owner or engineering firm that tracks capital projects in Planisware, export project_risk_score and compliance_calendar outputs (permit, Cal/OSHA, prevailing-wage milestones) as CSV for import as portfolio risks or milestones.

Where a customer has Planisware MCP on 26Q2+ in its enterprise AI client, a user could read a project's schedule milestones through it, then call construction_hours, check_cal_osha_permits and public_works_readiness for the matching California jobsite. This setup is unconfirmed.

mcp.note: No endpoint published; presumably specific to each customer.

status.note: MCP is 'available for all Planisware customers in version 26Q2 and above', per Planisware's resource page. Zapier separately offers a third-party Planisware Orchestra MCP with limited actions.

The description of Planisware as both an MCP server and an MCP client comes from a competitor (ITM Platform).

entries.name: Microsoft Project (MSPDI XML schedule import)
entries.summary: Microsoft Project desktop is the CPM scheduling tool many California GCs use for baseline and look-ahead schedules. It saves schedules in Microsoft's Project XML Data Interchange format (MSPDI) through File > Save As > XML Format (*.xml), defined by the Project XML Data Interchange Schema (mspdi_pj12.xsd).
details: Key Task fields in Microsoft's schema reference: UID (required, the permanent ID), ID (the row position), Name, Start, Finish, ActualStart, ActualFinish, CalendarUID (points to a Calendar in the Project's Calendars element) and PredecessorLink (PredecessorUID, Type FF/FS/SF/SS, LinkLag, LagFormat).
entries.tradecomply_role: Export your schedule as XML and upload it to TradeComply's schedule import, so lien, notice and Cal/OSHA permit deadlines line up with the dates in your schedule. It is a file you upload; TradeComply never connects to Microsoft.

builtin.what_it_does: Schedule import (being added to TradeComply): upload a Microsoft Project XML (MSPDI) or Primavera P6 export and TradeComply reads activity names and dates to place deadlines and safety checks next to the work.

uses.text: Import the GC's MSPDI schedule export. Use the ActualFinish (or planned Finish) of the completion milestone to drive calculate_lien_deadline and stop_payment_notice_deadline, and to put notice-of-completion follow-ups on compliance_calendar.

Scan Task Names and dates for excavation, trenching, scaffolding, demolition, crane or confined-space work. Run check_cal_osha_permits, confined_space_classification and jobsite_hazard_checklist ahead of each activity's Start.

Check activities scheduled for evenings or weekends against city noise limits with construction_hours and local_jobsite_requirements. In summer and fall, add wildfire_smoke_requirements and valley_fever_requirements for earthwork activities.

For Title 24 alterations, place energy_compliance_triggers (HERS verification) before the activity that closes the scope. Export TradeComply deadlines back as MSPDI Task elements the scheduler can import.

mcp.note: There is no official Microsoft Project MCP server. Microsoft documents a Planner MCP server (part of Work IQ) for basic plans only; its status and endpoint were not researched.

api.auth: Not applicable: a file the user exports and uploads.
notes: This is a file format, not an API. Parse MSPDI with a safe XML parser (defusedxml) to prevent XXE.
Exports use the default namespace http://schemas.microsoft.com/project (seen in exported files but not re-verified; confirm against a customer sample).
Join Task/CalendarUID to Calendars/Calendar/UID. Key tasks on UID, not ID: ID changes when rows are re-ordered. Duration values are ISO 8601-style strings (for example PT8H0M0S), not verified.
Microsoft notes that merging XML into an open project can lose data, so any write-back file should be a separate import. Tests should use small synthetic fixture files, not customer schedules.

gov.note: A file you export from your own copy of Project; no Microsoft cloud service is involved.
gov.label: No cloud service involved

status.label: Current product
status.note: Project desktop and Project Server Subscription Edition continue. Project Online retired 2026-09-30 (announced 2025-09-05 on Microsoft's Planner blog), with customers pointed to Planner or Project Server Subscription Edition.

caveats: The detailed element pages for ActualFinish, CalendarUID and PredecessorLink are the Project 2007 (mspdi_pj12) reference, marked 'no longer maintained'. The current Microsoft Learn alphabetical list still includes these elements.
Community MCP servers for Planner or Microsoft 365 are not Microsoft products.
Pricing was not researched.
research_notes: The Microsoft product page was not fetched. Schema facts come from Microsoft Learn and the MicrosoftDocs GitHub source.

entries.name: Oracle Primavera P6 (XER and P6 XML schedule import)
entries.summary: Primavera P6 is the CPM scheduler required on many public-works, utility and large commercial jobs. P6 exports two formats: XER (Oracle's proprietary, tab-delimited format covering project, resource and role data) and P6 XML, defined by Oracle's p6apibo.xsd schema.
details: XER TASK table fields per Oracle's XER Import/Export Data Map Guide: task_code (Activity ID), task_name (Activity Name), target_start_date (Planned Start), act_start_date (Actual Start), act_end_date (Actual Finish), clndr_id (Calendar, joins to the CALENDAR table) and early_start_date. P6 XML Activity elements include Id, Name, PlannedStartDate, StartDate, FinishDate, ActualStartDate, ActualFinishDate and CalendarObjectId.
entries.tradecomply_role: Export the schedule from P6 as XER or P6 XML and upload it to TradeComply's schedule import, so public-works lien and stop-payment deadlines, apprentice and prevailing-wage checks and Cal/OSHA permit checks line up with your activities. TradeComply never connects to Oracle.

builtin.what_it_does: Schedule import (being added to TradeComply): upload a Primavera P6 XER or P6 XML export (or a Microsoft Project XML file) and TradeComply reads activity names and dates to place deadlines and safety checks next to the work.

uses.text: On a public-works job, import the P6 XER. Use act_end_date of the completion or acceptance activity to compute stop_payment_notice_deadline and calculate_lien_deadline (public-works rules), and load the dates into compliance_calendar.

Use activity durations by trade to run apprentice_hours_required and prevailing_wage_penalties exposure for the planned labor. Run public_works_readiness before the first activity with an actual start.

Flag trench, shoring, crane, scaffold and confined-space activities by task_name and target_start_date. Then run check_cal_osha_permits, overhead_line_clearance, check_crew_certifications and confined_space_classification a week ahead.
For SCAQMD, SJVAPCD or BAAQMD jobs, attach dust_control_requirements to mass-grading activities, and offroad_contracting_requirements to activities that use off-road diesel fleets.
For federally funded work that requires a P6 schedule, pair the imported schedule with federal_project_requirements and davis_bacon_vs_ca_prevailing for each phase.

mcp.note: No first-party Oracle MCP server for Primavera was found. viaSocket sells a third-party 'Oracle Primavera Cloud MCP'.

api.auth: Not applicable for file import. P6 EPPM REST and Web Services run against the customer's own P6 server or Oracle cloud tenant; their auth was not researched.
notes: This is a file format, not an API. XER: read line by line and split on tabs; %T starts a table, %F gives its column names, each %R line is one record, %E ends the file, and the file begins with an ERMHDR line (UK National Archives PRONOM signature). Decode as Windows-1252 rather than UTF-8 (per third-party guides). Join TASK.clndr_id to CALENDAR.clndr_id. Use task_code as the user-facing Activity ID; check whether task_id is persistent against a sample.
P6 XML: use defusedxml; join Activity CalendarObjectId to Calendar ObjectId. The XML namespace is version-specific and was not verified.
Use synthetic fixture files, not customer schedules. Do not add a Java dependency (MPXJ needs a JVM) unless approved; a small native parser covers TASK, CALENDAR and PROJECT.

gov.note: A file you export from P6; no Oracle cloud service is involved.
gov.label: No cloud service involved

status.label: Current product
status.note: P6 Professional Version 26 is documented by Oracle.

caveats: The XER record syntax (%T, %F, %R, %E) and the Windows-1252 encoding come from third-party guides, not an Oracle format spec. Confirm both against a real customer export.
Oracle's data map excerpt did not show the target_end_date (Planned Finish), status_code or CALENDAR clndr_name / clndr_data mappings; treat those as unverified until the full Oracle PDF is read.
P6 XML element names come from MPXJ's classes generated from Oracle's p6apibo.xsd, which is not publicly downloadable: a faithful derivation, but not Oracle's own page.
research_notes: The Oracle Primavera product page was not fetched.

entries.name: Box (Box MCP Server)
entries.summary: Box hosts an MCP server so AI assistants (Claude, ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot Studio, GitHub Copilot, Mistral Le Chat and others) can search, read, upload and organize Box content and run Box AI over it, under each user's existing Box permissions. Tools include search_files_keyword, ai_qa_single_file, ai_qa_multi_file, ai_qa_hub, upload_file, create_folder, get_folder_details and list_folder_content_by_folder_id; some (upload_file_version, set_file_metadata and others) are off until an admin turns them on.
entries.tradecomply_role: Connect Box's MCP server and TradeComply's in the same AI assistant: read license numbers and insurance dates out of the paperwork in Box, check them with TradeComply, and file TradeComply's contracts and safety programs back into the job folder. A direct 'Save to Box' button in TradeComply is possible with Box's API but is not built yet.

uses.text: Prequalify subs from their paperwork. In Claude with TradeComply and Box both connected, run search_files_keyword for 'certificate of insurance' in the project's Subcontractors folder and use ai_qa_multi_file to extract each sub's CSLB license number, classification and CGL/workers' comp expiry. Feed the rows into TradeComply bulk_check_subcontractors, and run check_subcontractor_compliance on any sub whose insurance expires before the scheduled completion date.
Run TradeComply generate_home_improvement_contract for a residential remodel, then upload_file the result into the homeowner's job folder in Box so the PM and office work from one copy.

Audit a contract signed outside TradeComply. Use ai_qa_single_file on the signed PDF in Box to pull contract price, down payment, progress payment schedule and the date the buyer got the signed copy. Then run TradeComply validate_home_improvement_contract and home_improvement_cancellation_deadline.

Run TradeComply generate_safety_programs (IIPP, Code of Safe Practices, heat illness plan) for a new jobsite, then create_folder '<Job>/Safety' and upload_file the programs so the superintendent can open them from a tablet in the field.

Check payment terms across subcontracts. Use ai_qa_multi_file over the subcontract agreements in Box to extract retention percentage and pay-when-paid timing, then run TradeComply retention_cap_check and prompt_payment_check on each one.

Public works and federal jobs. Use ai_qa_hub on a Box Hub holding the bid specs to find Davis-Bacon or Buy America clauses, then run TradeComply federal_project_requirements, davis_bacon_vs_ca_prevailing and buy_america_check. File the public_works_readiness output back into the job folder.

mcp.note: The self-hosted open-source server (box-community/mcp-server-box) is marked deprecated in Box's developer docs; do not confuse its tool names (box_search_tool and others) with the hosted server's.

servers.label: Box MCP Server
servers.auth: OAuth 2.0 user sign-in. A Box admin enables the server (Admin Console > Integrations), creates Integration Credentials (client ID and secret) and registers the exact redirect URI your MCP client uses. Dynamic client registration is not supported. Scopes: root_readwrite, ai.readwrite and docgen.readwrite (docgen needs Enterprise Advanced).
servers.notes: Box's own Claude Code guide uses: claude mcp add box --transport http https://mcp.box.com. Claude's built-in Box connector avoids the admin-issued client step.

api.auth: Box Platform API: OAuth 2.0 authorization code grant per tenant (a Box 'OAuth 2.0' custom app in the Developer Console; client ID and secret in TradeComply environment variables; per-tenant access and refresh tokens stored encrypted).
notes: Possible future 'Save to Box' connector (not built). AUTHORIZE: send the user to https://account.box.com/api/oauth2/authorize?response_type=code&client_id={CLIENT_ID}&redirect_uri={REGISTERED_URI}&state={csrf}. redirect_uri must exactly match a registered URI (errors redirect_uri_missing, redirect_uri_mismatch).

TOKEN: POST https://api.box.com/oauth2/token (form) with grant_type=authorization_code, code, client_id, client_secret. The response includes access_token, expires_in (about 60 minutes) and refresh_token. REFRESH: the same URL with grant_type=refresh_token. Refresh tokens are single-use and valid 60 days, and each refresh returns a new one, so always store the newest; after 60 days unused the user must re-authorize.
SCOPES are set on the app in the Developer Console, for example root_readwrite ('Read and write all files and folders').

UPLOAD (50 MB or less): POST https://upload.box.com/api/2.0/files/content as multipart/form-data. The 'attributes' part (JSON {"name": "<file name>", "parent": {"id": "<folder_id>"}}) must come before the 'file' part, or the API returns 400 metadata_after_file_contents. Larger files use the Chunked Upload API. Preflight: OPTIONS https://api.box.com/2.0/files/content.
RATE LIMITS: 1,000 API requests per minute per user; 240 upload requests per minute per user; Box may impose temporary limits.

The folder-create endpoint (POST https://api.box.com/2.0/folders) and the file download endpoint were not re-verified; confirm them before coding. A customer's Box admin may have to approve a third-party custom app before users can authorize it (standard Box admin control, not re-verified).

gov.name: Box for Government (FedRAMP)
gov.note: Box holds FedRAMP Class D (High) certification (formerly 'FedRAMP High Authorized') and states GovRAMP High and CJIS alignment for state and local customers. Box's FedRAMP developer guide lists the same API hosts (account.box.com, api.box.com, upload.box.com, dl.boxcloud.com, realtime.services.box.net), so a direct API connection works there. Whether the hosted MCP server (mcp.box.com) is inside that boundary was not confirmed.
gov.label: Government cloud: partly

status.label: Generally available
status.note: Box support article 'Announcing the new remote Box MCP Server GA release (Aug 2025)' and the Box blog post 'The Box MCP server is now GA with Claude'. The Box Platform API (Content API v2.0) is Box's production API.

caveats: Plan eligibility conflicts across Box sources: the Aug 2025 GA note says Business plans and above; a later support article says all plans can connect but only use the tools their plan includes. Box AI tools (ai_qa_*) draw down Box AI Units (Enterprise includes 1,000 a month, Enterprise Plus 2,000, Enterprise Advanced 20,000; Business and Business Plus must buy units). Confirm with Box sales.
The claim that Box Hubs tools are limited to Enterprise and above comes from a Box community post, not official documentation; unconfirmed.

entries.name: Docusign (eSignature)
entries.summary: Docusign is the e-signature service many contractors and owners already use. Its eSignature REST API v2.1 creates and sends envelopes (documents, recipients and signature tabs), tracks status and pushes status changes through Docusign Connect webhooks. Docusign also hosts an MCP server (GA 2026-09-30) that lets AI assistants prepare, send, track and manage agreements.
entries.tradecomply_role: TradeComply's built-in Docusign connection sends documents TradeComply generated and checked (home improvement contracts, change orders, statutory lien waivers, subcontracts) for signature, and records when they're signed. Or use Docusign's own MCP server next to TradeComply's in your AI assistant.

builtin.what_it_does: Connects your Docusign account with OAuth (Authorization Code Grant). Planned uses: 'Send for signature' on TradeComply contracts, change orders and lien waivers, with completion dates recorded on the project.

uses.text: Add a one-click 'Send for signature' to TradeComply generate_home_improvement_contract output. TradeComply renders the PDF with anchor strings (for example /sn1/ and /ds1/ for the buyer, /sn2/ and /ds2/ for the contractor), creates the envelope with signHere and dateSigned tabs, and stores the envelopeId on the project.

Use the envelope-level Connect webhook. On envelope-completed, TradeComply records the completion date, runs home_improvement_cancellation_deadline (with buyer_age_65_or_older and disaster_repair taken from the project), and adds the last day to cancel to the project's compliance_calendar and project_setup_checklist.

Send change orders as envelopes after check_change_order passes, then re-run check_change_order with the signing dates from the signer completion events, so the office can see the order was fully signed before the changed work starts.
Send the select_lien_waiver statutory form to the sub, and hold the progress payment until envelope-completed arrives; time the release with prompt_payment_check.
Gate subcontract sending on bulk_check_subcontractors: only subs that pass license, classification and insurance checks get the subcontract envelope.

In Claude, run TradeComply generate_home_improvement_contract for the homeowner, then use Docusign's MCP 'Create Envelope with Documents' to send it, and 'Get Envelope' to confirm completion and feed the date the buyer received the signed copy into home_improvement_cancellation_deadline.
Accounts with Docusign IAM: use the Agreement Manager MCP tools to find signed subcontracts with retention clauses, then run TradeComply retention_cap_check on the extracted percentages.

mcp.note: Docusign's VS Code guide lists the connection type as HTTP; 'Streamable HTTP' is not stated verbatim on a page we could read. Claude custom-connector redirect URIs: https://claude.ai/api/mcp/auth_callback and https://claude.com/api/mcp/auth_callback ('Use your own OAuth client'). Workflow Builder and Agreement Manager tools need a Docusign IAM subscription.

servers.label: Docusign MCP Server (production)
servers.auth: OAuth 2.0. Official connectors (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Slackbot, Microsoft Copilot, Perplexity) reach production accounts. A custom connector uses your own Integration Key and secret, and using one against a production account requires Docusign's allowlist request form. Account admins can turn access off under Admin > Integrations > MCP Connections.
servers.notes: Connects to live accounts and real agreements. Not yet available for Government (FedRAMP) accounts; English only.

servers.label: Docusign MCP Server (demo)
servers.auth: OAuth with your own Integration Key from a free developer account.
servers.notes: Connects to a free developer account with test data only.

api.auth: OAuth 2.0 Confidential Authorization Code Grant per tenant user (with the 'extended' scope for a long-lived refresh token). JWT Grant suits service-style sending from one account but needs each customer's consent. Integration Key and secret in environment variables; per-tenant tokens, account_id and base_uri stored encrypted.
notes: HOSTS: auth server DEMO https://account-d.docusign.com, PRODUCTION https://account.docusign.com (one host for all production regions). Never hard-code the API base: use base_uri from /oauth/userinfo (demo is https://demo.docusign.net; production is data-center specific). REST root: {base_uri}/restapi/v2.1/accounts/{account_id}/.

AUTH CODE GRANT: set the Integration Key to Authorization Code Grant in Apps and Keys and register redirect URIs. Send the user to GET {auth}/oauth/auth?response_type=code&scope=signature%20extended&client_id={IK}&redirect_uri={registered}&state={csrf}. The code is valid about 2 minutes. Exchange it at POST {auth}/oauth/token (grant_type=authorization_code&code=..., HTTP Basic auth with IK:secret). With 'extended', each refresh returns a new refresh token with a full lifetime (typically 30 days); 'extended' is only grantable in the Auth Code flow.

JWT GRANT: claims iss={IK}, sub={user GUID}, aud='account-d.docusign.com' or 'account.docusign.com' (no https://), scope='signature impersonation', iat and exp, signed RS256. POST {auth}/oauth/token with grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer&assertion={jwt}. The token lasts 1 hour with no refresh token, and needs prior individual or org-admin consent.

USERINFO: GET {auth}/oauth/userinfo with Authorization: Bearer. Pick the accounts[] entry with is_default=true (or the tenant-selected account_id). Cache it: userinfo is rate-limited per user and per Integration Key.

CREATE ENVELOPE: POST {base_uri}/restapi/v2.1/accounts/{account_id}/envelopes with JSON {emailSubject, documents: [{documentBase64, name, fileExtension: 'pdf', documentId: '1'}], recipients: {signers: [{email, name, recipientId: '1', routingOrder: '1', tabs: {signHereTabs: [{anchorString: '/sn1/', anchorUnits: 'pixels', anchorXOffset: '0', anchorYOffset: '0'}], dateSignedTabs: [{anchorString: '/ds1/', ...}]}}]}, status: 'sent'} ('created' saves a draft). Anchors match every occurrence of the string, so keep them unique.

ENVELOPE-LEVEL CONNECT (all plans; account-level Connect only on certain plans): add eventNotification with url (https only), requireAcknowledgment, events ['envelope-sent', 'envelope-delivered', 'envelope-completed', 'envelope-declined', 'envelope-voided'] and eventData {format: 'json', version: 'restv2.1', includeData: [...]}. Verify HMAC by computing HMAC-SHA256 over the raw body with each Connect key, base64-encoding it, and comparing against X-DocuSign-Signature-1..N. Return 200 within 100 seconds or the message goes to the retry queue.

LIMITS: 3,000 API calls per hour per account by default; burst 500 per 30 s in production and 200 per 30 s in demo; poll any single envelope at most once per 15 minutes (or use Connect). Polling violations can fail Go-Live review. Read the X-RateLimit-* and X-BurstLimit-* headers.

GO-LIVE: promote the Integration Key to a paid production account (Docusign's FAQ says Business Pro or higher; free trials cannot go live). Review is automatic or manual (typically 24 to 48 hours). This is Docusign's standard Go-Live, not partner-program approval.

gov.note: Docusign's MCP server does not cover Government (FedRAMP) accounts yet. Docusign's government environment for the eSignature API was not researched.

status.note: MCP server GA on 2026-09-30 per Docusign's developer blog (open beta before that; some older pages still say beta). eSignature REST API v2.1 is Docusign's current production API.

entries.name: Google Workspace (Gmail, Drive, Calendar)
entries.summary: Google's productivity suite: Gmail, Drive, Calendar, Docs, Sheets, Meet and Chat. Google now hosts one MCP server per product for AI agents. The Gmail server can search, read, label and draft email (it has no send tool: a person reviews and sends each draft). The Drive server can search, read, copy and create files.
entries.tradecomply_role: Connect Google's Gmail and Drive MCP servers and TradeComply's in the same AI assistant: read sub paperwork and owner emails, check them with TradeComply, and draft replies or save results to Drive. For deadlines on your Google Calendar, use TradeComply's built-in calendar feed (no Google sign-in needed).

uses.text: In Claude, search_threads for 'certificate of insurance' or 'COI' from subcontractors, then get_thread to read the license number and expiry. Run TradeComply verify_contractor_license and check_subcontractor_compliance, then create_draft a request for an updated COI to any sub that fails. The office reviews and sends it.

search_threads for homeowner emails asking for extra work, then run TradeComply check_change_order on the requested change and create_draft a reply explaining that a written change order signed by both parties is needed before the work starts.
search_threads for employee leave requests sent to the office, run TradeComply leave_request_check (or sick_leave_status), and create_draft the response for HR to send.

search_threads for preliminary notices or stop payment notices received from suppliers, run TradeComply stop_payment_notice_deadline and calculate_lien_deadline, and label_thread them 'Lien deadlines' with the computed date in a draft note to the PM.
After an injury email comes in from the field, run TradeComply injury_reporting_deadlines and create_draft the internal escalation to the safety manager with the due times.

In Claude, search_files for the 'Subcontractor list' sheet in the job folder, read_file_content, and pass the rows to TradeComply bulk_check_subcontractors. Then create_file a 'Sub prequal results' doc in the same folder.
read_file_content on a draft home improvement contract in Drive and run TradeComply validate_home_improvement_contract to list missing headings and notices before it goes to the homeowner.
Run TradeComply generate_safety_programs for a new jobsite and create_file the IIPP and heat illness plan as Google Docs so the foreman can open them on a phone.

read_file_content on the owner's scope-of-work document, then run TradeComply classification_for_scope, permit_required, energy_compliance_triggers and calgreen_and_stormwater to build the pre-bid checklist.
download_file_content on crew certification PDFs (CDPH lead, electrician certification, crane operator cards), then run TradeComply check_crew_certifications before mobilizing.

mcp.note: Google also lists Docs, Sheets, Slides, Chat, People, Tasks and Classroom servers and a Universal Search server; those were not individually checked. Quotas: Standard Tier (free) is 5,000 requests per day per project per product. Scaled Tier needs billing, and Gmail, Calendar and Drive MCP billing starts 2027-04-01 (Google lists $0.10 to $0.50 per 1,000 billable requests by tier).

servers.label: Gmail MCP server
servers.auth: OAuth 2.0 with your own Google Cloud OAuth client: enable gmailmcp.googleapis.com in a Google Cloud project and create a Web application client with 'Use this client for an AI-powered agent' selected (required since 2026-11-12 per the Gmail release notes). The consent-screen scopes in Google's guide (gmail.readonly, gmail.compose, gmail.modify) are restricted scopes. In Claude, add a custom connector and enter the client ID and secret under Advanced settings.
servers.notes: No send tool and no attachments in create_draft yet; create_draft takes plain email addresses only.

servers.label: Google Drive MCP server
servers.auth: OAuth 2.0 with your own Google Cloud OAuth client: enable the Google Drive API and the Drive MCP API (drivemcp.googleapis.com) and select 'Use this client for an AI-powered agent'. Setup guide scopes: drive.readonly (restricted) and drive.file (non-sensitive).
servers.notes: Tools: search_files, list_recent_files, get_file_metadata, get_file_permissions, read_file_content, download_file_content, copy_file, create_file.

servers.label: Google Calendar MCP server
servers.auth: OAuth 2.0 with your own Google Cloud OAuth client.
servers.notes: Listed in Google's Workspace MCP guide; its own configuration page was not read in our research.

api.auth: A possible future direct connector would use a Google OAuth web-server client (access_type=offline) with per-tenant refresh tokens stored encrypted.
notes: OAUTH (web server): GET https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth?client_id=...&redirect_uri=...&response_type=code&scope=...&access_type=offline&state=...; exchange at POST https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token. The refresh_token is only returned with access_type=offline. Apps left in 'Testing' publishing status get refresh tokens that expire after 7 days.

SCOPE STRATEGY (avoid restricted scopes): Drive https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.file is non-sensitive (files the app creates or the user picks). Calendar events.insert accepts calendar, calendar.events, calendar.app.created or calendar.events.owned; prefer calendar.app.created (its sensitivity label was not confirmed). Gmail gmail.send is sensitive: OAuth verification but no third-party security assessment. Avoid gmail.readonly, gmail.compose, gmail.modify, drive and drive.readonly: they are restricted and need a security assessment at least every 12 months if data is stored on servers (internal-only apps are exempt).

DRIVE UPLOAD (5 MB or less): POST https://www.googleapis.com/upload/drive/v3/files?uploadType=multipart, multipart/related, metadata part first ({"name", "parents": [folderId], "mimeType"}), then the media part; larger files use a resumable upload. CALENDAR: POST https://www.googleapis.com/calendar/v3/calendars/{calendarId}/events with an Event JSON (summary, description, start.date/end.date for all-day deadlines). GMAIL SEND: users.messages.send with body {"raw": base64url(RFC 2822 MIME)}; it costs 100 quota units, and for projects created on or after 2026-05-01 the limit is 6,000 units per minute per user per project.
Google's quota page says that from 2027-02-01 'AI agents' calling the REST APIs directly are held to Standard Tier quotas; confirm how Google classifies server-side button flows.
While a Workspace MCP server is in Developer Preview, Google's program terms say preview features may not be included in public applications before GA.

gov.note: Google Workspace FedRAMP or government offerings were not researched for this catalog.

The Gmail MCP server has no send or attachment support, so a person reviews and sends every email.

entries.tradecomply_role: Use alongside TradeComply when your jobsite addresses, payroll exports or sub lists live in Google Cloud: look up a jobsite's city and county with Maps, then run TradeComply's local rules for it, or query a week of timecards in BigQuery and check them with TradeComply.

uses.text: Jobsite rules lookup. Use Maps Grounding Lite (place search and routes) to confirm which city and county a new jobsite address falls in. Then call local_jobsite_requirements, construction_hours, valley_fever_requirements and dust_control_requirements for that site. Grounding Lite's exact tool names were not confirmed.

Payroll from a data warehouse. A mid-size GC whose timecards land in BigQuery queries one week's hours per worker through the BigQuery MCP. The rows go to check_payroll and, on federal jobs, to federal_overtime_exposure and davis_bacon_vs_ca_prevailing.
Sub roster in Google Sheets. Read the subcontractor sheet with Google's open-source Workspace server (a Gemini CLI extension) and pass it to bulk_check_subcontractors before awarding packages.
Job files in Cloud Storage. Confirm through the Cloud Storage MCP that the job's bucket holds the current generate_safety_programs output and the signed generate_home_improvement_contract PDF.

entries.name: Splunk (audit-log export and Splunk MCP Server)
entries.summary: Splunk is a security and observability platform (Splunk Cloud Platform or self-managed Splunk Enterprise). Its HTTP Event Collector (HEC) is a token-authenticated HTTPS endpoint that accepts JSON events. Splunk also makes the Splunk MCP Server app (Splunkbase app 7931), which exposes Splunk search and metadata to AI clients on your own Splunk deployment.
entries.tradecomply_role: TradeComply's built-in Splunk export sends your company's TradeComply activity log (who ran which check, when, and whether the answer was verified) to your own Splunk through HEC, for an independent, searchable copy. Then the Splunk MCP Server lets your AI assistant search that history.

builtin.what_it_does: Sends each TradeComply activity-log row (company, user, tool, summarized inputs, verified, result, source, time) to the HEC URL, token and optional index your Splunk admin gives you. Being added to TradeComply.

uses.text: Stream every MCP/API tool call (check_payroll, prevailing_wage_penalties, apprentice_hours_required, bulk_check_subcontractors) into the GC's Splunk. This gives an independent, tamper-resistant record for SOC 2, cyber-insurance or awarding-body questionnaires.

Build a Splunk dashboard of verified=false results by tool, such as calculate_lien_deadline and stop_payment_notice_deadline. A compliance manager then reviews unverified answers before lien or stop-payment deadlines go out.
Alert in Splunk when field-role users trigger 401/403 errors on office-only pages, or when the anonymous /mcp demo sees unusual volume.
Keep a searchable history of which superintendent ran injury_reporting_deadlines or wildfire_smoke_requirements on which date, in case Cal/OSHA asks during an inspection.

With both MCP servers loaded, a CA public-works GC's office asks Claude 'who ran check_payroll or prevailing_wage_penalties for Project X in October'. Claude runs splunk_run_query over the TradeComply audit index, then re-runs public_works_readiness before a DIR or awarding-body review.

Run splunk_run_query for TradeComply tool calls where verified=false in the last 30 days, then re-check each answer with get_california_rule or search_california_rules before relying on it in a bid or contract.
Use splunk_list_fired_alerts to review alerts on spikes of rejected TradeComply /mcp API keys (401s), then revoke the key in TradeComply Settings > AI assistant (MCP).
Correlate when the payroll clerk ran sick_leave_status or final_paycheck_deadline against the HR termination date, as evidence in a Labor Code waiting-time penalty dispute.

mcp.note: Tools per the 2.1 docs: splunk_run_query (SPL and SPL2), splunk_get_info, splunk_get_index_info, splunk_get_user_info, splunk_list_alerts, splunk_list_fired_alerts and splunk_get_knowledge_objects. They run with the token user's permissions.

servers.label: Splunk MCP Server app (your Splunk)
servers.transport: HTTPS on your own Splunk deployment
servers.auth: An MCP encrypted token created in the Splunk MCP Server app, sent as 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' (a regular token from Settings > Tokens does not work). Token authentication must be on, and the user needs the mcp_tool_execute capability. OAuth 2.1 + PKCE sign-in on Splunk Cloud Platform is a beta preview (AWS regions only, no dynamic client registration).
servers.notes: Management-port form from the Cisco DevNet listing of app 1.0.x. Copy the exact endpoint and sample client config from inside the MCP Server app; the Splunk Cloud URL format is unconfirmed. Never copy sample configs that set NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0: that turns off TLS verification.

api.auth: HEC token (GUID) in the header 'Authorization: Splunk <token>'.
notes: No partnership needed: the customer's Splunk admin creates an HEC token and gives TradeComply the URL, the token and an optional index. Store all three per tenant, encrypted.

ENDPOINTS. Splunk Cloud: https://http-inputs-<stack>.splunkcloud.com/services/collector/event on port 443 (per a Splunk Community answer and Splunk ITE Work docs); trial and self-managed stacks use 8088. Splunk Enterprise: https://<host>:8088/services/collector/event. Raw text goes to /services/collector/raw. Health check: GET /services/collector/health (seen in a community post).
AUTH: 'Authorization: Splunk <hec_token>'. Basic auth and a ?token= query parameter also exist; don't use the query-string form, which leaks into proxy logs.

BODY: POST JSON such as {"time": <epoch seconds>, "host": "tradecomply", "source": "tradecomply:mcp", "sourcetype": "tradecomply:audit", "index": "<optional; must be allowed for the token>", "fields": {flat index-time fields}, "event": {audit row}}. All metadata keys are optional. Batch by concatenating JSON objects in one POST. The sourcetype and source values are TradeComply's own naming, not Splunk-defined.

RESPONSES: success is HTTP 200 {"text": "Success", "code": 0}; only code 0 was seen in the docs extract. Re-verify the rest of the status-code table on Splunk's 'Troubleshoot HTTP Event Collector' page before coding.

INDEXER ACK: if enabled on the token, each request needs X-Splunk-Request-Channel: <GUID>. Splunk docs say Splunk Cloud supports ack only for Amazon Data Firehose, so require ack-disabled tokens on Splunk Cloud.
RELIABILITY: keep TLS verification on; queue and retry on 503 and network errors; make it idempotent with an audit-id field; never block the MCP call.

There is an open-source version you run yourself (GA) and an Okta-hosted Managed MCP Server (Early Access).
entries.tradecomply_role: Use it next to TradeComply when onboarding or offboarding staff: Okta handles the accounts, TradeComply handles California rules such as the final-paycheck deadline. For signing in to TradeComply with Okta, see Single sign-on.

uses.text: Offboarding a superintendent or foreman: Okta MCP lists the person's app assignments and deactivates them (with confirmation). In the same Claude session, final_paycheck_deadline gives the California final-pay timing, and an office admin revokes the person's TradeComply API key.
Before a public-works audit, list members of the Okta 'Payroll' group and compare them with the TradeComply users who ran check_payroll or prevailing_wage_penalties (from TradeComply's activity log).
After a phishing scare at a jobsite trailer, pull Okta system-log failed logins for field users, then re-run jobsite_hazard_checklist or generate_safety_programs only from verified accounts.

When onboarding a new estimator, create the Okta user and add them to the 'Estimating' group, then confirm in TradeComply that they can run permit_required, estimate_permit_fees and classification_for_scope.
