entries.name: Single sign-on (OIDC): Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Google
entries.summary: Let your team sign in to TradeComply with your company's identity provider using OpenID Connect (authorization code with PKCE). Your IT admin creates an OIDC web app in the identity provider and enters its issuer, client ID and client secret in TradeComply. When someone leaves and is turned off in your identity provider, they can no longer sign in to TradeComply.
details: Okta's OIDC setup was researched for this catalog. Microsoft Entra ID and Google Workspace use the same OpenID Connect standard, but their specific setup steps were not researched here, so follow their documentation.
entries.tradecomply_role: Built in: TradeComply redirects your users to your identity provider, checks the signed ID token, and can map identity-provider groups to TradeComply roles (owner, office, field). No Okta partnership or app-catalog listing is needed.

builtin.what_it_does: Single sign-on for the TradeComply web app (being added). Your admin enters the issuer URL, client ID and client secret; TradeComply reads the issuer's discovery document rather than hard-coding any provider.

uses.text: The GC's office manager turns on SSO so PMs, payroll clerks and safety managers sign in with company credentials. An identity-provider group such as 'TC-Office' maps to the TradeComply office role (which can run check_payroll, prevailing_wage_penalties and compliance_calendar); 'TC-Field' maps to field (jobsite_hazard_checklist, wildfire_smoke_requirements and field logs in the offline app).

When HR deactivates a laborer or superintendent in the identity provider, their next TradeComply sign-in fails, so former employees can't pull project data or generate_home_improvement_contract drafts.
For public-agency work, an Okta for Government tenant can be the identity provider: the connector reads the issuer from discovery rather than assuming okta.com.
Require MFA in your identity provider before office users can create TradeComply API keys used by AI agents for bulk_check_subcontractors.

api.auth: OIDC Authorization Code + PKCE (S256), with a confidential client using client_secret_basic or private_key_jwt.
notes: PER-TENANT CONFIG (encrypted at rest): issuer, client_id, client_secret, group-to-role map, allowed email domain.

ISSUER AND DISCOVERY (Okta). Org authorization server: issuer https://{yourOktaDomain}, discovery https://{yourOktaDomain}/.well-known/openid-configuration, endpoints under /oauth2/v1/. Custom authorization server: issuer https://{yourOktaDomain}/oauth2/{authServerId} (the built-in one is 'default'), discovery /oauth2/{authServerId}/.well-known/openid-configuration, endpoints under /oauth2/{authServerId}/v1/. Always read authorization_endpoint, token_endpoint and jwks_uri from discovery, and check that discovery's issuer exactly equals the configured issuer.

AUTHORIZE: GET {authorization_endpoint}?response_type=code&client_id=...&redirect_uri=<TradeComply callback>&scope=openid%20profile%20email[%20groups]&state=<random>&nonce=<random>&code_challenge=<BASE64URL(SHA256(verifier))>&code_challenge_method=S256. TOKEN: POST {token_endpoint} form-encoded with grant_type=authorization_code, code, redirect_uri, code_verifier; authenticate with client_secret_basic, or private_key_jwt if configured.
VALIDATE the ID token: RS256 signature against jwks_uri keys (cache by kid), iss, aud == client_id, exp/iat, and nonce.

SCOPES (Okta): openid, profile, email, address, phone, offline_access and groups are documented for both server types. On the org server, 'groups' uses the app's Groups-claim filter but only in the ID token, and a 'thin' ID token omits profile and groups, so call /userinfo. On a custom server, create a 'groups' scope and claim yourself, otherwise the request fails with invalid_scope.
Okta enforces per-endpoint rate limits; exact values were not confirmed.

gov.name: Okta for Government
gov.note: Works with any standards-based OIDC issuer your admin enters, which can include Okta for Government High (FedRAMP High since March 2023, per an Okta press release). Government org domains differ from okta.com (exact domains unconfirmed).
gov.label: Government cloud: partly

status.note: OIDC Authorization Code + PKCE is a long-standing GA Okta flow.

caveats: Custom authorization servers may need Okta's API Access Management SKU in production orgs (unconfirmed), so support the org authorization server as the default.
Okta forum replies suggest a confidential web app can use a client secret without PKCE; using PKCE (S256) plus the secret is still recommended.

Endpoint patterns come from search extracts of Okta's 'Authorization servers' page, 'Authorization Code with PKCE' guide and groups-claim guide; the /oauth2/default/v1/authorize path is the documented pattern, not quoted verbatim.

entries.name: CrowdStrike Falcon MCP
entries.summary: CrowdStrike's falcon-mcp connects AI agents to the Falcon platform: detections, hosts, threat intel, NGSIEM queries, Spotlight vulnerabilities, Identity Protection, Cloud Security, Fusion SOAR, read-only RTR triage, policies, firewall, quarantine and Zero Trust Assessment. It can be narrowed with --modules, --read-only and tool filters. CrowdStrike says new work now ships in its hosted CrowdStrike MCP.
entries.tradecomply_role: For contractors already on CrowdStrike: check the security of the office and jobsite-trailer computers that handle payroll and federal paperwork, alongside TradeComply's labor and contract checks. Falcon data is outside TradeComply's compliance domain, so there is no built-in connector.

uses.text: Before submitting certified payroll or running check_payroll on a public-works job, the office runs falcon_search_detections and falcon_search_hosts (with --read-only) to confirm the payroll clerk's PC has no open detections.

For an awarding agency's or owner's cybersecurity questionnaire during public_works_readiness or project_setup_checklist, pull Zero Trust Assessment scores and Spotlight vulnerability counts for office and jobsite-trailer laptops.
When final_paycheck_deadline is triggered for a departing superintendent, check his laptop in Falcon Hosts and confirm it is contained or recovered.
For cyber-insurance renewal, summarize the past quarter's detections alongside TradeComply's compliance_calendar renewal deadlines.

servers.label: falcon-mcp (runs on your computer)

servers.notes: Docker image quay.io/crowdstrike/falcon-mcp:latest. The optional streamable-http transport is unauthenticated by default, so --api-key is mandatory when bound beyond the local machine.

entries.name: Palo Alto Networks Prisma AIRS MCP Server
entries.summary: Prisma AIRS exposes Palo Alto Networks' AI runtime security as MCP tools: pan_inline_scan (scan a prompt and/or response and get allow or block), pan_batch_scan (1 to 25 requests) and pan_get_scan_results. Detections cover prompt injection, sensitive data (DLP), URL categorization, toxic content and malicious code.
entries.tradecomply_role: For a GC already licensed for Prisma AIRS: have your AI assistant scan outside documents (pasted COIs, emailed license claims) before feeding them to TradeComply checks, and scan payroll exports for sensitive data before they leave the company.

uses.text: In a Claude workspace used by the office, run pan_inline_scan on subcontractor-supplied text (pasted COIs, bid notes, emailed license claims) before feeding names into bulk_check_subcontractors or verify_contractor_license. This screens for prompt-injection payloads in third-party documents.
Use pan_inline_scan's sensitive-data detection on a certified-payroll export before sending it to check_payroll through a third-party AI client, so SSNs or bank numbers don't leave the company.
Scan an AI-drafted response that combines generate_home_improvement_contract output with outside web content before it goes to a homeowner.

Require the two-stage scan (user input first, then the response with the prompt) in the company AI policy for any agent that chains TradeComply tools such as public_works_readiness and prevailing_wage_penalties with email or Slack actions.

servers.label: Prisma AIRS MCP Server (US)
servers.auth: A Prisma AIRS API key generated in Strata Cloud Manager, sent in the x-pan-token header, or an OAuth 2.0 access token from Strata Cloud Manager. An optional x-pan-profile header selects the AI security profile.
servers.notes: Regional variants use service-de, service-in and service-sg subdomains (exact hostnames to confirm). Seen through search extracts of Palo Alto's docs.

For reference: POST https://service.api.aisecurity.paloaltonetworks.com/v1/scan/sync/request with header x-pan-token and JSON {"tr_id", "ai_profile": {"profile_name"}, "metadata", "contents": [{"prompt", "response"}]}; limits 2 MB per sync request and 100 URLs per request; an async endpoint /v1/scan/async/request also exists. The response field schema is unconfirmed.

entries.name: Arcade MCP Runtime and Gateways
entries.summary: Arcade hosts prebuilt MCP servers and lets a project combine tools from several servers, including remote servers you register, into one gateway URL. It curates the allowed tools per gateway, handles each user's OAuth sign-ins and token refresh, and keeps upstream tokens out of the AI client. The open-source arcade-mcp framework builds custom servers.
entries.tradecomply_role: Register TradeComply's remote MCP in an Arcade project next to Arcade's Google, Microsoft or Slack tools, so one gateway can run TradeComply checks and then act on the results (calendar events, Slack posts, emails) under each user's own sign-in.

uses.text: Register TradeComply's remote MCP (https://missed-call-recovery-n1c3.onrender.com/mcp) as a remote server in an Arcade project alongside Arcade's Google or Microsoft tools. A PM's single gateway can then run compliance_calendar and create the resulting deadlines as calendar events.
In the same gateway, post a weekly digest of compliance_calendar and stop_payment_notice_deadline dates to a Slack channel through Arcade's Slack tools.
Run generate_safety_programs or jobsite_hazard_checklist, then email the result to the superintendent through Arcade's Gmail or Outlook tools under that user's own OAuth grant.

Curate an 'Estimating' gateway exposing only permit_required, estimate_permit_fees, classification_for_scope and verify_contractor_license, and a separate 'Payroll' gateway with check_payroll, prevailing_wage_penalties and apprentice_hours_required.

servers.label: Your Arcade gateway
servers.auth: 'Arcade Auth': users sign in through Arcade with OAuth (User Sources can delegate to your company's OIDC identity provider). 'Arcade Headers': 'Authorization: Bearer <arcade_api_key>' plus 'Arcade-User-ID: <end_user_id>' on every request, recommended only for dev, test or internal use.
servers.notes: One URL per gateway, created in the Arcade dashboard. Docs recommend fewer than 80 tools per gateway.

api.auth: Not applicable: Arcade consumes TradeComply as a remote MCP server.
notes: Open question: whether Arcade's 'add remote servers' flow can send a static per-user 'Authorization: Bearer <TradeComply key>' upstream, or needs OAuth. TradeComply's /mcp only supports static API keys today, so test this before relying on it.

Pair TradeComply with Barndoor's Xero integration: an AP clerk runs prompt_payment_check and retention_cap_check, then looks up the matching Xero bills under one audited identity.
Use Barndoor's approval gate before an agent emails a lien waiver selected by select_lien_waiver to a subcontractor.
Use Barndoor DLP to stop payroll files used with check_payroll from going to an unapproved AI model.

entries.summary: An enterprise gateway between AI clients and MCP servers: sign-in, a log of every tool call (user, tool, server, guardrail result) exportable to a SIEM, and access policies. It can host local servers as remote ones and groups curated tools into 'Virtual MCP' bundles mapped to roles. The company announced its rename to Mintive on Oct 12, 2026.

Export gateway logs to the GC's Splunk, next to TradeComply's own audit export, for a joint review of who ran bulk_check_subcontractors before a subcontract award.
Combine TradeComply with the gateway's hosted Okta MCP connector, so an admin offboarding a user can also run final_paycheck_deadline in one governed session.
Give field superintendents a mobile-friendly Virtual MCP limited to jobsite_hazard_checklist, wildfire_smoke_requirements, valley_fever_requirements and overhead_line_clearance.

entries.name: Slack (channel alerts and Slack MCP Server)
entries.summary: Slack is team messaging. Incoming webhooks post a message to one channel when you send an HTTPS POST to the webhook's secret URL. Slack also hosts an MCP server (GA since 2026-02-17) that lets AI assistants search messages and files, send and schedule messages, read channels and threads, and work with canvases and Lists, under each user's permissions.
entries.tradecomply_role: Built in: paste a Slack incoming-webhook URL into TradeComply and it posts compliance alerts (deadlines coming up, license or sub problems, injury reports due, payroll issues) to that channel. Or use Slack's MCP server next to TradeComply's in your AI assistant.

builtin.what_it_does: Posts TradeComply alerts to a Slack channel through an incoming webhook. The URL is stored encrypted and never shown again; you can send a test message any time.

uses.text: Each morning, post the TradeComply deadline dashboard items for the next 14 days (preliminary notices, lien recording and foreclosure dates, license and COI expiries) to #compliance.

When a verify_contractor_license recheck shows a subcontractor's CSLB license as expired or suspended, post an alert naming the sub and the jobs it is on, with a link to unlicensed_contracting_exposure output.
Post stop_payment_notice_deadline and calculate_lien_deadline countdowns to the PM's project channel before each date.
After bulk_check_subcontractors runs on a new job's sub list, post a one-line summary (X clear, Y with problems) with a link to the full report in TradeComply.
When check_payroll or prevailing_wage_penalties flags a certified-payroll problem on a public works job, post it to #payroll so it is fixed before the weekly submission.

In Claude with both the Slack MCP and TradeComply MCP connected, search the job channel for superintendent messages about added scope or field directives, then run check_change_order on each one to flag change orders missing the written terms California home-improvement change orders require.
When a foreman posts an AQI reading in #field, run wildfire_smoke_requirements for that reading and reply in the thread with the respirator and communication duties it returns.
Paste project_setup_checklist output into a Slack canvas in a new project channel so the office manager and PM can check off permits, notices and insurance together.

mcp.note: Community 'Slack MCP' servers that use session tokens get around admin approval; don't use them. MCP calls count against the same Web API rate-limit tiers as direct API calls.

servers.label: Slack MCP Server
servers.auth: OAuth 2.0 user tokens through a registered Slack app; dynamic client registration is not supported (Slack's official plugin ships a pre-registered client). A workspace admin must approve the MCP integration before users can sign in. Scopes per tool group, for example search:read.public, chat:write, canvases:read and canvases:write.
servers.notes: Only Slack Marketplace apps and internal apps may use the MCP server. Slack's official Claude Code plugin (slackapi/slack-mcp-plugin) is the simplest setup.

api.auth: Incoming webhooks: the secret URL is the credential (stored encrypted per tenant).
notes: Request: POST {webhook_url} with Content-Type: application/json. Body {"text": "..."} or {"text": "fallback", "blocks": [...]}; always send a top-level text as the notification fallback with blocks. Success is HTTP 200 with body 'ok'. Each URL posts only to the channel it was created for (python-slack-sdk docs).

Rate limit: 1 request per second with short bursts allowed; HTTP 429 with Retry-After when exceeded (Slack rate-limits page, search summary). Errors (Slack's 2016 incoming-webhook error changelog, search summary): invalid_payload (400, fix before retrying), no_service or no_active_hooks (webhook removed or disabled), channel_is_archived (410). TradeComply turns a webhook off on 410 and on those Slack codes.
Do not build a server-side connector on the Slack MCP server: only Marketplace and internal apps may use it, so calling it from TradeComply's servers would need a Marketplace listing.

gov.name: GovSlack
gov.note: GovSlack runs on the separate domain slack-gov.com (FedRAMP High and DoD IL4, per Slack). Slack's developer page says the Slack MCP server is not yet supported on GovSlack, and GovSlack incoming-webhook URLs were not confirmed. TradeComply's Slack alerts accept only hooks.slack.com URLs.

status.note: Incoming webhooks are a long-standing GA feature. Slack MCP Server GA since 2026-02-17 per Slack's blog and changelog (seen as search summaries). Slack's Claude Code plugin is at version 1.8.0.

Slack's error codes and the 1-per-second limit come from search summaries; re-read them on docs.slack.dev.

entries.name: Microsoft Teams (Workflows webhook alerts)
entries.summary: The Teams Workflows app (built on Power Automate) gives you a webhook URL through the 'When a Teams webhook request is received' trigger or templates such as 'Send webhook alerts to a channel'. Posting JSON to it makes the workflow post a message or Adaptive Card to a channel (private channels included) or chat. It replaces the Office 365 connector incoming webhooks, which Microsoft retired in May 2026.
entries.tradecomply_role: Built in: create the workflow in Teams, paste its URL into TradeComply, and TradeComply posts its compliance alerts as Adaptive Cards with a button back to TradeComply.

builtin.what_it_does: Posts TradeComply alerts to a Teams channel or chat through a Workflows webhook, as an Adaptive Card. The URL is stored encrypted.

uses.text: Post an Adaptive Card each morning to the project team's Teams channel listing TradeComply dashboard deadlines due in 14 days (preliminary notices, lien recording dates, license and COI expiries), with a button to each item.

When verify_contractor_license or check_subcontractor_compliance finds a sub's license or insurance problem, post a card naming the sub, the jobs affected and the fix, so the PM holds the sub's start.
Post check_crew_certifications gaps (for example missing forklift or crane operator certifications) to the safety channel before the crew mobilizes.
Post the public_works_readiness checklist and check_payroll results to a public-agency job's Teams channel before each certified-payroll submission.

mcp.note: A Microsoft Teams MCP server exists only in preview, per search summaries (mcp_TeamsServer in Microsoft Agent 365, and the 'Work IQ' MCP). Not verified, so no endpoint is listed.

api.auth: Depends on the trigger's 'Who can trigger the flow?' setting. 'Anyone': anyone with the URL can post, and requests must not carry a token. 'Any user in my tenant' or 'Specific users in my tenant': an Entra ID bearer token with audience https://service.flow.microsoft.com/ (public cloud).
notes: Setup: the customer creates the workflow (channel menu > Workflows > 'Send webhook alerts to a channel', or a flow with the 'When a Teams webhook request is received' trigger) and pastes the generated URL into TradeComply, where it is stored encrypted.

Adaptive Card body: {"type": "message", "attachments": [{"contentType": "application/vnd.microsoft.card.adaptive", "contentUrl": null, "content": {"$schema": "http://adaptivecards.io/schemas/adaptive-card.json", "type": "AdaptiveCard", "version": "1.2", "body": [...]}}]}. Supported actions include Action.OpenUrl, Action.ShowCard and Action.ToggleVisibility (not Action.Submit). Card text supports basic Markdown; HTML shows as plain text.
Limits: message size 28 KB; more than 4 requests per second is throttled (connector table: 4 per second, 60 per 30 s, 100 per hour, 150 per 2 hours, 1,800 per day). Back off on 429.

URL changes: since 2025-11-30 the old logic.azure.com trigger URLs no longer work, and since 2026-06-02 new URLs include a scale-unit segment (/direct/cu/<n>/workflows/...). Store whatever URL the customer pastes; never hard-code a host.

Authenticated mode (option): the tenant registers an Entra app, lists its service principal under 'Specific users in my tenant', and the sender gets a client-credentials token for https://service.flow.microsoft.com/ (or the government audience). The exact success status code was not confirmed; treat any 2xx as success.

entries.name: Signed webhooks (Standard Webhooks)
entries.summary: Send TradeComply alerts to any HTTPS endpoint your developer or automation tool runs. Every message follows the open Standard Webhooks specification: a JSON body {type, timestamp, data} with webhook-id, webhook-timestamp and webhook-signature headers, signed with HMAC-SHA256 using a secret TradeComply shows you once, so the receiver can prove the message came from TradeComply.
entries.tradecomply_role: Built in: for teams with their own systems (an ERP, a data warehouse, an automation tool such as Workato). Failed deliveries are retried on a schedule, and the delivery log shows what was sent.

builtin.what_it_does: Posts each chosen TradeComply event to your HTTPS endpoint, signed per Standard Webhooks. Retries for about three days with backoff; a 410 Gone answer turns the webhook off.

uses.text: Send deadline_due_soon and sub_noncompliant events to your own system so it can open a task or hold a payment, and verify each message's signature with any Standard Webhooks library.
Point the webhook at an automation tool's HTTP trigger (for example a Workato recipe) that files bulk_check_subcontractors results or compliance_calendar dates into your other systems.
Send injury_report_due events to the safety manager's paging or ticketing tool so the injury_reporting_deadlines clock is never missed.

api.auth: HMAC-SHA256 signature in the webhook-signature header (v1,<base64>), with a whsec_ secret of 32 bytes shown once at creation or rotation.
notes: Receivers verify with any Standard Webhooks library, or TradeComply's app.webhooks.verify(secret, headers, body). Signed content: '{id}.{timestamp}.{body}'. The webhook-id stays the same on every retry, so receivers can drop duplicates.

gov.note: You run the receiving endpoint, wherever you need it.
gov.label: No cloud service involved

status.label: Open specification
status.note: Standard Webhooks is an open specification with reference libraries in many languages.

caveats: TradeComply only calls public HTTPS addresses (ports 443 or 8443) and does not follow redirects for signed webhooks.
research_notes: The Standard Webhooks spec was read through Context7 when the webhook sender was built.

entries.name: Twilio (SMS text alerts)
entries.summary: Twilio's Programmable Messaging REST API sends SMS and MMS from a Twilio number or Messaging Service, reports delivery status through status-callback webhooks, and receives replies including STOP and HELP. Twilio also hosts a no-sign-in MCP server that searches Twilio's documentation and API specs (Public Beta).
entries.tradecomply_role: Built in: connect your company's own Twilio account so TradeComply can text urgent alerts to opted-in foremen, crew leads and PMs. US texting from ordinary 10-digit numbers requires A2P 10DLC registration in your Twilio account first.

builtin.what_it_does: Texts TradeComply alerts from your own Twilio account to people who opted in. Being added to TradeComply.

uses.text: When wildfire_smoke_requirements returns an AQI at or above the threshold for a jobsite, text opted-in foremen and crew leads the required protective steps, sent through a Messaging Service registered under an A2P 10DLC campaign.

When check_subcontractor_compliance or bulk_check_subcontractors finds a sub's workers' comp or license expired, text the sub's office contact (with consent) that they cannot start until it is fixed, and log the message ID on the sub record.
After a reported injury, text the safety manager the injury_reporting_deadlines result (for example the Cal/OSHA serious-injury reporting clock), with a link back to TradeComply.

Send a homeowner an informational reminder of the cancellation date from home_improvement_cancellation_deadline. This is a reminder only; the statutory written notice must still be in the generate_home_improvement_contract document.
Text the PM 2 days before a stop_payment_notice_deadline or calculate_lien_deadline date that falls on a weekend, so it is filed in time.

For your developer: with the Twilio docs MCP server connected, look up A2P 10DLC campaign requirements (opt-in wording, HELP/STOP, sample messages) for 'jobsite safety alerts', and check CreateMessage field rules with twilio__retrieve.

mcp.note: Community Twilio MCP servers in the MCP registry are not Twilio's.

servers.label: Twilio MCP (documentation and API-spec search)
servers.auth: None: no API key or Twilio account needed.
servers.notes: Two tools: twilio__search and twilio__retrieve. It cannot send messages. Public Beta, not covered by Twilio's support terms or SLA.

servers.label: Twilio Alpha MCP Server (proof of concept, runs on your computer)
servers.auth: Account SID plus an API Key SID and secret on the command line.
servers.notes: A proof of concept by Twilio's ETI team that can send messages and spend money. Prefer a Restricted API key limited to Messages, and load a narrow tool set (--services twilio_api_v2010).

api.auth: HTTP Basic auth: Account SID and Auth Token, or (recommended) an API Key SID (SK...) and secret, with the Account SID in the URL path. Restricted keys can be limited to specific resources.
notes: SEND: POST https://api.twilio.com/2010-04-01/Accounts/{AccountSid}/Messages.json, form-encoded, Basic auth (operationId CreateMessage in twilio_api_v2010.json). Required: To (E.164); exactly one of From or MessagingServiceSid; at least one of Body, MediaUrl or ContentSid. Body up to 1,600 characters, split into segments over 160 GSM-7 or 70 UCS-2 characters, each billed. Optional: StatusCallback, ValidityPeriod (1 to 36000 s), SendAt with ScheduleType=fixed (Messaging Service only), MessageIntent, RiskCheck.

RESPONSE: 201 JSON Message resource; sid matches ^(SM|MM)[0-9a-fA-F]{32}$; status one of accepted, scheduled, canceled, queued, sending, sent, failed, delivered, undelivered, receiving, received, read, partially_delivered; error_code null unless failed or undelivered (Twilio says not to rely on it programmatically). Fetch: GET /2010-04-01/Accounts/{AccountSid}/Messages/{Sid}.json.

STATUS CALLBACKS: Twilio POSTs form-encoded MessageSid, MessageStatus, ErrorCode and more on each status change; ignore unknown fields. Validate X-Twilio-Signature with Twilio's RequestValidator (built with the Auth Token, so a tenant using only API keys must also supply the Auth Token, or TradeComply polls instead). Answer 204 or an empty <Response/>.

ERRORS to handle: 21211 invalid To, 21408 geo permission, 21610 recipient opted out (never retry), 30003 unreachable, 30007 carrier filtered, 30034 unregistered 10DLC sender, 30450 SMS pumping blocked.

US A2P 10DLC is required for all US 10DLC senders: Customer Profile (Trust Hub), Brand (EIN; Sole Proprietor brands are Console-only), Campaign (use case, 2+ sample messages with opt-out text, message-flow/opt-in description, privacy policy, terms with HELP/STOP, 'Message and data rates may apply' and frequency), then link numbers through a Messaging Service. Toll-free numbers need Toll-Free Verification instead.

OPT-OUT: Twilio handles STOP, STOPALL, UNSUBSCRIBE, CANCEL, END and QUIT by default, added REVOKE and OPTOUT on 2025-05-14 (changelog, search summary), and handles START and HELP. TradeComply must also keep its own per-number consent record and stop sending on 21610.

Recommended model: each company brings its own Twilio account (Account SID, API Key SID and secret, Messaging Service SID, optional Auth Token), encrypted per tenant, so TradeComply does not register as an ISV. Twilio Test Credentials make calls without charges or real sends.

status.label: Generally available (SMS API)
status.note: Twilio REST API 2010-04-01 is GA. The docs MCP server is Public Beta. Compliance Toolkit features (quiet hours, reassigned-number checks) are Public Beta per Twilio's skills repo.

caveats: Safety and compliance alerts are informational but still need the recipient's prior express consent. Get legal review before texting homeowners.
Campaign review timelines and per-tier daily limits come from Twilio's skills repo, not a primary help page; treat them as unconfirmed.
Twilio's messaging-services skill shows a MessageIntent value ('confirm') that is not in the API spec; follow the spec.
No pricing was gathered.
research_notes: www.twilio.com and help.twilio.com could not be fetched during our research. API details come from Twilio's official OpenAPI spec (github twilio/twilio-oai); compliance details come from Twilio's official skills repo (github twilio/ai, Public Beta content) and search summaries. A third-party directory claims the docs MCP server uses OAuth; Twilio's own README says no authentication, and the official source wins.

entries.name: Zoom MCP Server (Zoom Workspace)
entries.summary: Zoom hosts an MCP server for Zoom Workplace data: AI Companion meeting search, meeting assets and summaries, recordings and transcripts, Team Chat and Canvas search, and creating Zoom Docs. Useful results need AI Companion features (Smart Recording, Meeting Summary) turned on and a paid Zoom plan.
entries.tradecomply_role: Connect Zoom's MCP server next to TradeComply's in your AI assistant: pull what was agreed in an owner or sub meeting, then check it with TradeComply (change orders, insurance, safety topics).

uses.text: After the weekly owner-architect-contractor (OAC) Zoom meeting, use search_meetings and get_meeting_assets to pull the AI Companion summary, then run check_change_order on each scope change discussed and record what still needs a signed change order.
Pull the transcript of a recorded tailgate or toolbox safety meeting with get_recording_resource and compare it against generate_safety_programs output to note which required topics were covered.
Create a Zoom Doc (create_new_file_with_markdown) holding project_setup_checklist and permit_required results for a new job, then share it from the kickoff meeting.
Search past sub coordination meetings for promises about insurance certificates, then run check_subcontractor_compliance on those subs to see what is actually on file.
Turn action items from a homeowner pre-construction meeting into a follow-up doc alongside home_improvement_cancellation_deadline and construction_hours results for the address.

servers.label: Zoom Workspace MCP server
servers.auth: User OAuth bearer token from a user-managed General App on marketplace.zoom.us: authorization code flow (PKCE where the client can't keep a secret) at https://zoom.us/oauth/authorize, token exchange at https://zoom.us/oauth/token. Access tokens last about an hour. Dynamic client registration is not supported (per Zoom's docs, search summary), so client registration is manual.

notes: Not a backend connector: a General App used outside the creating account needs Zoom Marketplace publishing (not confirmed), and the MCP surface is per-user OAuth. For deterministic meeting create/update/delete, Zoom's skill says to use the Zoom REST API.

entries.name: Calendar feed for Google Calendar and Outlook
entries.summary: A private calendar link (an iCalendar .ics feed) with your company's deadlines: preliminary notices, lien recording and foreclosure dates, license and insurance certificate expiries, and toolbox talks. Subscribe to it once in Google Calendar, Outlook or Apple Calendar and the deadlines show up on everyone's phone, read-only, with a 7-day reminder on lien, notice, license and COI items.
entries.tradecomply_role: Built in, no sign-in to Google or Microsoft needed: copy the link from TradeComply and add it as a calendar 'from URL' (or 'subscribe from web'). Make a new link any time to cut off old copies.

builtin.what_it_does: Your company's deadline calendar as a private .ics link. Anyone with the link can see the deadlines and project names, so keep it private.

uses.text: The PM and office manager subscribe to the company's TradeComply feed so preliminary notice, mechanics lien recording, lien foreclosure, license expiry and COI expiry dates from the deadline dashboard show up next to their job calendars.
Add compliance_calendar annual filings (payroll tax, Cal/OSHA postings, license renewal) to the feed, so the bookkeeper sees them in Outlook.
When calculate_lien_deadline or stop_payment_notice_deadline is run for a job, save the result as a project deadline so it shows up on the feed within the calendar app's refresh window.
Put retention_cap_check and prompt_payment_check due dates for public works pay applications on the feed for the accounts-receivable clerk.

api.auth: A secret token in the link (calendar apps can't send a sign-in). Rotate it from TradeComply to cut off old copies.
notes: Each event has a stable UID, so an updated date changes the event in place instead of adding a duplicate. Lines end in CRLF and are folded at 75 octets; served as text/calendar. Google fetches from its own servers, so the feed must be public HTTPS.

gov.note: Your calendar app fetches the feed from TradeComply. Whether your organization's calendar allows subscribing to outside calendars depends on your admin settings.
gov.label: No cloud service involved

status.label: Available in TradeComply
status.note: The feed is live in TradeComply. RFC 5545 is the iCalendar standard (2009).

caveats: Calendar apps refresh subscribed calendars on their own schedule, which is commonly reported to take hours or more than a day (Google and Microsoft refresh behavior was not confirmed). Don't rely on the feed alone for same-day or next-day legal deadlines: also turn on Slack, Teams or text alerts.
The link is a secret: anyone with it sees your deadlines and project names. Don't share it; make a new link if it leaks.
webcal:// links are a convention, not a registered scheme (unverified); use the https:// link if webcal doesn't work.
research_notes: rfc-editor.org, support.google.com and support.microsoft.com could not be reached during our research, so the RFC details and refresh behavior were not re-read.

entries.name: AWS MCP Server and AWS MCP servers (awslabs)
entries.summary: AWS hosts a managed AWS MCP Server that makes authenticated calls to AWS APIs in your own AWS account (aws___call_aws, aws___run_script, documentation search, presigned S3 URLs and more), using IAM SigV4 signing through AWS's local proxy. AWS Labs' open-source awslabs/mcp suite runs single-service servers locally, and the AWS Knowledge MCP server searches AWS documentation with no account needed.
entries.tradecomply_role: For contractors with federal or DoD work whose files live in AWS: check how drawings and records are stored, next to TradeComply's federal labor and contracting checks. TradeComply does not cover CMMC or DFARS cybersecurity rules; AWS's tools give infrastructure facts only.

uses.text: USACE or NAVFAC bid. Run federal_project_requirements to get the labor, E-Verify, SAM and Buy American clauses TradeComply covers. TradeComply does not cover the DFARS cybersecurity/CMMC clauses; for those, start the AWS MCP Server proxy with --read-only under an IAM policy limited to read actions and have Claude inventory the S3 buckets holding the solicitation's drawings, reporting default encryption and Block Public Access settings as input to the firm's System Security Plan.

Records retention. After check_payroll and, on federal jobs, federal_overtime_exposure produce a week's results, call aws___get_presigned_url for a pre-signed S3 upload URL and file the exported result in the job's records bucket.

Sub roster at scale. A GC whose subcontractor list is a CSV in S3 has aws___run_script read it; Claude then passes the text to bulk_check_subcontractors for CSLB license, workers' comp and bond flags before a pre-bid meeting.

Hosting CUI drawings. An IT lead deciding where a DoD solicitation's CUI drawings may be stored uses AWS Knowledge MCP (no AWS account needed) to read current AWS GovCloud (US) documentation, next to the federal_project_requirements and project_setup_checklist output for the same job.

mcp.note: The awslabs servers (aws-documentation, aws-iac, aws-pricing, cloudwatch, dynamodb and others) run locally over stdio with uvx; SSE was removed 2025-05-26. The IAM, Kendra Index, Amazon Q Business and Cloud Control API servers are deprecated, and the AWS API MCP Server is superseded by the managed server.

servers.label: AWS Knowledge MCP (documentation, no account needed)
servers.auth: None ('does not require authentication but is subject to rate limits').
servers.notes: Tools: search_documentation, read_documentation, list_regions, get_regional_availability.

servers.label: AWS MCP Server (managed, your AWS account)
servers.transport: Remote HTTP with SigV4, reached through AWS's local stdio proxy
servers.auth: IAM SigV4 using the standard AWS credential chain (environment, credentials file, profiles, roles); the proxy takes --profile and --read-only. IAM condition keys can allow an agent only read actions even if the user's role can write; CloudTrail records every request.
servers.notes: A plain URL won't work in an AI client: it needs the SigV4 proxy. AWS's migration guide pins mcp-proxy-for-aws@1.6.3 and advises against @latest; the proxy README shows the mcp-proxy-for-aws-cli package. A Frankfurt endpoint (https://aws-mcp.eu-central-1.api.aws/mcp) appears in search results only.

api.auth: IAM SigV4.
notes: Not a built-in candidate: a direct connector would mean holding each tenant's AWS credentials or cross-account roles inside TradeComply, which is high-risk for little compliance value.

gov.name: AWS GovCloud (US)
gov.note: Nothing we read says the managed AWS MCP Server is available in AWS GovCloud (US).
gov.label: Government cloud: unconfirmed

status.label: Generally available (managed server)
status.note: Preview announced Nov 2025; GA on 2026-05-06 per an AWS What's New post (search snippet). The Agent Toolkit for AWS repo carries a GA badge, and the awslabs README recommends it for production. AWS Knowledge MCP GA in Oct 2025 (search result).

TradeComply has no CMMC or DFARS cybersecurity coverage; these servers give infrastructure facts, not compliance determinations.
The awslabs servers act with whatever IAM permissions the configured profile has; IAM is the primary control and READ_OPERATIONS_ONLY is only an extra layer.
The GA date, Regions and 'no additional charge' pricing come from search snippets (pricing from a third-party summary only).

entries.name: Azure MCP Server
entries.summary: Microsoft's MCP server for Azure resources (45+ service areas, including Storage, Key Vault, Azure Monitor log queries, Azure Database for PostgreSQL, App Service, Azure Policy, Advisor, AKS, Cosmos DB and SQL). It runs on your computer (or self-hosted) with your Azure sign-in, has a --read-only mode, and can target Azure US Government with --cloud AzureUSGovernment.
entries.tradecomply_role: For contractors with an Azure Government enclave for federal work: check storage, Key Vault expiry dates and policy compliance next to TradeComply's federal labor checks and renewal deadlines. TradeComply never holds Azure credentials.

uses.text: DoD-bound sub with an Azure Government enclave for CUI: start the server with --cloud AzureUSGovernment --read-only and the storage, keyvault and policy namespaces. Have Claude list the enclave's storage accounts and Azure Policy compliance state, alongside federal_project_requirements output for the same solicitation, as one bid-readiness checklist.

One renewal list. Pull Key Vault certificate and secret expiry dates through Azure MCP and merge them with compliance_calendar output (CSLB license expiration, payroll tax and city business tax dates) so the office manager gets a single dated list.

CMMC evidence requests. When an assessor asks for sign-in or activity evidence, use Azure Monitor log queries through Azure MCP, paired with TradeComply's labor-side evidence from check_payroll and federal_overtime_exposure for the same federal job. TradeComply itself has no CMMC coverage.

Job file check. List blobs in the job's storage container to confirm that the current IIPP and heat-illness programs from generate_safety_programs, and the signed contract from generate_home_improvement_contract, were filed for the project.

mcp.note: The old repo github.com/Azure/azure-mcp is archived; development moved to github.com/microsoft/mcp. Microsoft also hosts Azure Resource Manager MCP (https://mcp.management.azure.com, preview, can create and deploy resources) and Microsoft Learn (https://learn.microsoft.com/api/mcp).

servers.label: Azure MCP Server (runs on your computer)
servers.auth: Azure Identity credentials (az login locally; EnvironmentCredential in Docker). In self-hosted HTTP mode, Entra ID authenticates incoming requests; never use --dangerously-disable-http-incoming-auth.
servers.notes: Pin a stable version: npm's 'latest' tag currently points to a beta (4.0.0-beta.10). Add --cloud AzureUSGovernment for Azure US Government.

api.auth: Azure Identity (Entra ID).
notes: Not a built-in candidate: it runs in the customer's environment with the customer's Entra identity.

gov.name: Azure US Government
gov.note: The server targets sovereign clouds with --cloud AzureUSGovernment (or AZURE_CLOUD=AzureUSGovernment). Confirm your AI client is allowed to handle CUI before using it against a GCC High or Azure Government enclave.

status.note: npm @azure/mcp 1.0.0 (2025-10-28), 2.0.0 (2026-04-10, Microsoft's 'stable release' post), 3.0.0 stable (2026-10-12).

Azure Resource Manager MCP (remote, preview) can create resources and deployments; Microsoft suggests an Azure Policy to block create_deployment.

entries.name: Secureframe hosted MCP server
entries.summary: Secureframe is a compliance automation (GRC) platform for SOC 2, ISO 27001, CMMC, FedRAMP and other frameworks. Its hosted MCP server gives AI assistants access to your Secureframe data: controls, tests, personnel, devices, vendors, frameworks and integrations, under each user's Secureframe permissions.
entries.tradecomply_role: For a contractor tracking CMMC or SOC 2 in Secureframe: put Secureframe's cyber controls next to TradeComply's California and federal labor and licensing checks in one AI conversation. Secureframe is the system of record for cyber controls; TradeComply is for labor and licensing.

uses.text: Bid-readiness memo. A DoD-bound GC tracking CMMC in Secureframe asks Claude, with both servers connected, to list failing tests and unhealthy controls for the CMMC framework, next to federal_project_requirements output for the same solicitation: one memo covering the cyber clauses and the labor and E-Verify clauses.

Combined sub prequal. List the Secureframe vendors the firm tracks for CUI flow-down (for example risk_level:High), and run bulk_check_subcontractors on the same companies for CSLB license, workers' comp and bond status.

Departing employee. Use Secureframe's personnel list to confirm the employee's system access was removed, and call final_paycheck_deadline for the same employee so the office meets the California Labor Code deadline.

servers.label: Secureframe MCP (US)
servers.auth: OAuth sign-in from the MCP client the first time it connects, or an API key for a user whose permissions match the intended tasks. Access follows the user's Secureframe roles.
servers.notes: UK: https://mcp-uk.secureframe.com/. Whether the MCP path is the root or /mcp is unconfirmed. Developer docs: https://mcp.secureframe.com/mcp_docs.

api.auth: Secureframe REST API: header 'Authorization: <API_KEY> <API_SECRET>' (key and secret separated by a space, not 'Bearer').
notes: A built-in connector is optional and not recommended now. If built later: base URL https://api.secureframe.com (US) or https://api-uk.secureframe.com (UK); keys are created under Company Settings > API keys and the secret is shown once. GET endpoints used by Secureframe's archived server: /controls, /tests, /users, /devices, /frameworks, /vendors (legacy), /tprm/vendors, /integration_connections, /user_accounts, /repositories, with page, per_page (default 100), q (Lucene, e.g. health_status:fail) and include parameters. Not confirmed: rate limits, response envelope and pagination fields, write endpoints, CMMC framework key names.

status.label: Available (no GA label confirmed)
status.note: Secureframe's launch blog 'Now Available: Hosted MCP Server' is dated 2026-08-05 (search snippet). The earlier self-hosted server was a public beta with 11 read-only tools; its repo says it is no longer maintained and was archived 2026-07-17.

caveats: The hosted server includes write tools; use a least-privilege Secureframe user or API key.
Tool counts differ between Secureframe's blog and support article, so none are repeated here.
TradeComply's rulebook does not cover CMMC.

entries.name: OWASP MCP Top 10
entries.summary: The OWASP project that ranks MCP-specific security risks (a living document; 2025 list): MCP01 Token Mismanagement and Secret Exposure, MCP02 Privilege Escalation via Scope Creep, MCP03 Tool Poisoning, MCP04 Software Supply Chain Attacks, MCP05 Command Injection, MCP06 Prompt Injection via Contextual Payloads, MCP07 Insufficient Authentication and Authorization, MCP08 Lack of Audit and Telemetry, MCP09 Shadow MCP Servers, MCP10 Context Injection and Over-Sharing.
details: Related OWASP material: the MCP Security Cheat Sheet (least privilege per server and tool, don't trust tool descriptions, sandbox local servers, never auto-approve tool calls without showing the full parameters), the GenAI Security Project's 'A Practical Guide for Securely Using Third-Party MCP Servers' v1.0, and OWASP AISVS chapter C10 'MCP Security'.
entries.tradecomply_role: A checklist for your IT or security reviewer before connecting any MCP server to your AI assistant, TradeComply's included.

uses.text: Give your IT or security reviewer the OWASP MCP Top 10 as the checklist for every MCP server you connect to your AI assistant, TradeComply's included.
Create a separate TradeComply API key for each AI assistant or gateway, so the activity log shows which one ran each check, and revoke keys you no longer use (MCP01 token handling, MCP08 audit).

Treat text that comes back from tools as untrusted when an assistant chains results into email or Slack actions: sub names, project names and CSV notes in bulk_check_subcontractors or project_setup_checklist output come from other people (MCP06, MCP10).
Register every TradeComply MCP endpoint your company uses (the hosted /mcp and any local install) with your security team, so they're inventoried rather than shadow servers (MCP09).

status.label: Living document
status.note: MCP Top 10 version '2025'. The OWASP project page shows a 'Production' classification while other sources describe it as beta or v0.1.

An 'MCP Security Minimum Bar' checklist is attributed to an OWASP GenAI guide by vendor blogs only; it is not confirmed in the primary document.
The GenAI third-party MCP guide is dated Oct 23, 2025 by one source and Nov 4, 2025 by another.

entries.name: Bulwark Agent Security (Python library)
entries.not_recommended_reason: A small beta library (2 releases, nothing since June 2026) whose README contradicts its own code; reference only.
entries.summary: An Apache-2.0 Python library that wraps agent tool handlers in a five-layer pipeline: input sanitizer, injection detector (22 regex signatures plus an optional DeBERTa model), role-by-tool access control (default deny), a human approval gate, and an encrypted audit trail. Its 'MCP integration' is an in-process wrapper, not a network proxy or MCP server.
entries.tradecomply_role: Reference only, for comparing agent-guardrail designs. Not for production use with TradeComply.

uses.text: Compare its audit design with TradeComply's activity log when reviewing OWASP MCP08 (audit and telemetry) for your own AI agents.

Prototype only: run its injection signatures over free-text fields in subcontractor CSVs before bulk_check_subcontractors results are echoed into an AI conversation. Regex detection is easy to bypass, so treat it as defense in depth at most.

notes: Read from the 0.2.0 wheel source (downloaded from PyPI and inspected without running it): the audit trail uses Fernet (AES-128-CBC with HMAC-SHA256) while the README says 'AES-128 GCM'; default audit storage is in-memory; BulwarkMCPProxy needs each handler registered by hand.

entries.not_recommended_reason: Deprecated on npm and archived (2026-04-15); its data source is FedRAMP's legacy documentation repo.
entries.summary: A community MCP server that indexed FedRAMP's documentation repository (21 tools for FedRAMP requirements, controls and guidance). Every version is deprecated on npm ('migrated to grclanker.com and myctrl.tools') and the repo was archived on 2026-04-15. It says it is not affiliated with FedRAMP or the U.S. government.
entries.tradecomply_role: Not recommended. FedRAMP authorizes cloud services sold to federal agencies; it does not certify contractors. A contractor's own federal cyber program is CMMC, which this server does not cover. For whether a cloud vendor is authorized, use the FedRAMP Marketplace.

uses.text: After federal_project_requirements flags a direct federal or DoD contract, the question is whether your cloud vendors are authorized for the data. Check the FedRAMP Marketplace or FedRAMP's official rules repo, not this deprecated server.

status.label: Deprecated
status.note: Latest 0.2.6 (2026-04-15); every version carries an npm deprecation notice. The official MCP Registry still lists 0.2.2 as active.

caveats: Its upstream, FedRAMP/docs, is now titled 'FedRAMP Legacy Documentation' and warns it is not a source of truth for current FedRAMP rules, so answers from this server are stale by design.
research_notes: www.npmjs.com returned HTTP 403 to our fetcher, so the public npm registry JSON API was read instead. The server was not run.

entries.name: FedRAMP 20x MCP Server (community)
entries.not_recommended_reason: Community project whose documented data source now returns 404; FedRAMP 20x applies to cloud providers, not contractors.
entries.summary: A community MCP server (MIT license, v1.3.0 on PyPI, 2026-02-13) with 48 tools for querying FedRAMP 20x requirements and running compliance-pattern analysis on code (Python, C#, Java, TypeScript/JavaScript, Bicep, Terraform), with Azure-first guidance. Nothing indicates it is official from FedRAMP, GSA or Microsoft.
entries.tradecomply_role: Not applicable to contractors: FedRAMP 20x is for cloud service providers seeking federal authorization. Your federal labor and contracting obligations come from TradeComply's federal tools.

uses.text: A California GC or sub bidding DoD work deals with CMMC, not FedRAMP 20x; use TradeComply's federal_project_requirements, buy_america_check, davis_bacon_vs_ca_prevailing and federal_overtime_exposure for the labor and contracting side.
